topics.title: Common chargers and USB-C
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Core facts
- A common charging interface improves interoperability and reduces charger purchases and e-waste; USB-C identifies the connector, not a guarantee of identical charging speed.
- EU rules apply to specified rechargeable radio equipment from **28 December 2024**; laptops follow from **28 April 2026**. Covered categories include phones, tablets, cameras, headphones, handheld consoles, speakers, e-readers, keyboards, mice, navigation devices and earbuds. [EU Council](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/infographics/2022-06-07-common-charger-directive/).
## India and implementation
- The supplied January 2025 notes describe consultations beginning in 2022 and a proposed June 2025 phone/tablet deadline, followed by laptops in 2026. **Treat these Indian dates as source-reported proposals pending notification verification.**
- Benefits: reusable chargers, lower consumer costs, simpler inventories, less waste and easier international compatibility.
- Challenges: redesign costs, industry resistance, legacy devices, clear power-rating information and consumer awareness. Complement standardisation with repair, refurbishment and formal recycling.

topics.title: Coffee cultivation, heritage and exports
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Idukki plantation history
- Pallikkunnu CSI Church near Kuttikkanam, Kerala, preserves an old coffee tree associated with colonial plantation history.
- Source account: British expansion in the early 19th century; coffee initially dominant around **Peerumade, Kuttikkanam and Thengakal**; leaf disease in **1875** encouraged a shift towards tea.
- The source reports a roughly 150-year-old tree and historical Thengakal yields of 2 tonnes/acre; these are local heritage claims requiring independent corroboration.
## Mains links
- Plantation economies show how disease, crop suitability and profitability reshape land use and livelihoods.
- Preserve agricultural heritage through cultural tourism; diversify crops and strengthen pest/climate resilience.
## Exports: January 2025 report
- **Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu** are major growing states; Karnataka leads. Europe is a key market: Italy, Belgium and Germany; other destinations include US, Russia and UAE.
- Higher Robusta prices and supply disruptions in Brazil/Vietnam can lift export value; distinguish price-driven receipts from volume growth. The source links pre-EUDR stockpiling to demand.
- Source's 'first ever $1 billion' claim and mixed April-November/FY labels are unreliable: official data show **$1.29 billion in FY2023-24**. [PIB coffee brief](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/jan/doc2025120487201.pdf).
- **EUDR** means traceable deforestation-free supply chains; costs include documentation and monitoring. Avoid assuming every Indian exporter necessarily violates it or that the EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation applies uniformly to every coffee consignment.
- Mains: value-added exports, farmer incomes, diversification, climate/pest resilience, sustainable sourcing and trade compliance.

topics.title: Manufactured sand
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Meaning and policy context
- **M-sand**: sand-size aggregate produced by crushing suitable rock, including granite/basalt, often using a **Vertical Shaft Impact (VSI)** crusher.
- Source context: Rajasthan M-Sand Policy 2024 seeks to reduce dependence on river sand and encourage sustainable construction.
## Benefits and limits
- Reduces riverbed disturbance, erosion, groundwater impacts and habitat damage from excessive extraction.
- Controlled processing can improve grading and consistent supply; suitable mine overburden may provide feedstock after quality testing.
- Cost and construction performance depend on rock quality, processing and transport. **Do not memorise the source's blanket claim that M-sand needs no washing:** fines removal and treatment may be necessary.
## Way forward
- Enforce grading/quality standards; invest in local processing and logistics; offer appropriate incentives and research support; demonstrate performance to builders; support alternative livelihoods for affected mining workers.

topics.title: E-waste and extended producer responsibility
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Core facts
- E-waste is discarded electrical/electronic equipment. Hazardous constituents include **lead, mercury, cadmium, chromium and beryllium**.
- **EPR** shifts end-of-life responsibility towards producers; collection, authorised recycling and certificate systems help implement obligations.
- The source reports 2024 amendments enabling EPR-certificate trading; verify the applicable category and target rather than assuming a uniform 25% recycling obligation.
## January 2025 source figures
- Generation: **1.751 million tonnes in 2023-24**, reported increase **72.54%**; recycled share **43%**, untreated share **57%**. The comparison year and statistical definitions need verification.
- Source also cites 65 cities generating 60% and 10 states generating 70%; baseline years are unspecified.
## Risks and response
- Unsafe informal dismantling/burning contaminates air, soil and water and exposes workers. Landfilling can leach toxins; uncontrolled incineration releases hazardous emissions.
- Priorities: take-back points, authorised recyclers, worker training and formalisation, repair/reuse/refurbishment, better recovery technology, public awareness and enforcement.
- **Basel Convention**: hazardous-waste transboundary movement; **Minamata Convention**: mercury. Domestic links include hazardous-waste regulation and circular-economy policy.
## PYQ trap
- UPSC Prelims 2013: beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury and lead are the relevant listed substances; answer **(b)**. The full question is in the common Environment PYQ file.
- PYQ recall: **EPR was an important feature of the e-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011**; distinguish the historical rule asked in 2019 from later replacement rules.

topics.title: Operation Greens
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Purpose and scope
- Launched **2018** by the **Ministry of Food Processing Industries**: improve producer returns, stabilise prices for producers/consumers, reduce post-harvest losses and build processing capacity.
- Initially **TOP = Tomato, Onion, Potato**. Budget 2021-22 expanded long-term coverage to **22 perishables, including shrimp**. [MoFPI/PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1744337&lang=2&reg=48).
- Supports value-chain infrastructure, farmer-producer organisations, storage, transport, processing and cluster-to-market links; short-term support and long-term projects should be distinguished.
## Parliamentary review reported in January 2025
- Source reports **34% of Rs 59.44 crore** allocated for 2024-25 spent by October 2024, alongside Maharashtra onion-price falls and potato shortages. Preserve the reporting period; do not present these as current figures.
- Bottlenecks: unused funds, inadequate cold chains, stakeholder coordination, export-policy uncertainty and weather/supply shocks.
## Mains framework
- Producer income + consumer affordability require predictable trade decisions, timely funding, market intelligence, efficient logistics and accountable implementation.

topics.title: Lead pollution and public health
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Exposure and effects
- Lead is a toxic metal; exposure comes from unsafe battery recycling, paints, contaminated products, occupational dust and legacy pollution. Geological weathering is a natural source.
- Children are especially vulnerable: impaired brain development, learning and behaviour; other effects include anaemia, kidney damage, hypertension and reproductive harm.
- **No known safe blood lead level.** A 5 micrograms/dL action threshold is not a safety boundary. [WHO guidance](https://www.who.int/news/item/27-10-2021-who-guidance-to-reduce-illness-due-to-lead-exposure).
- India phased out leaded petrol by 2000, but contamination can persist.
## Regulation and response
- **Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022** replaced the **Batteries (Management and Handling) Rules, 2001**. They cover multiple battery categories and use EPR for collection/recycling/refurbishment. The source's title 'Lead Battery Waste Management Rules (2016)' is incorrect. [MoEFCC/PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1854433&lang=2&reg=48).
- Priorities: safer products, formal recycling, occupational protection, child/pregnancy screening, pollution monitoring/remediation and reliable exposure data.
## Source figures requiring baseline checks
- January 2025 PDFs cite 275 million exposed children, 4.6 million DALYs and 165,000 annual deaths, but omit the underlying study years/thresholds.
- They identify Bihar, UP, MP, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh as high-burden states and cite a 40% share with unclear denominator. Keep these as unverified source estimates, not a definitive state ranking.

topics.title: Sea-level rise and coastal adaptation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Causes and consequences
- Ocean warming causes **thermal expansion**; melting **land ice** adds ocean water. Ocean circulation and land subsidence/uplift affect regional relative sea level.
- Impacts: inundation, erosion, saltwater intrusion, freshwater/crop damage, displacement, waterborne disease and fishing/tourism losses.
- Indian examples: Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Sundarbans mangroves and Odisha's olive-ridley nesting beaches.
## Adaptation
- Risk-sensitive coastal zoning/CRZ enforcement; early warnings and evacuation; climate-resilient infrastructure; mangrove restoration; context-appropriate protection and managed retreat; saline-tolerant agriculture.
## Climate target distinction
- India's 2022 updated NDC aimed for about **50% of cumulative installed electric-power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030**. This is not 50% of all energy use or necessarily of electricity generation. [Official NDC explanation](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1913467&lang=2&reg=48).
## Quantitative caution
- Source estimates (~20 cm rise since 1880, rate increasing from ~2 to ~4 mm/year, 1.2 m by 2100, 80% Sundarbans loss) lack consistent periods/scenarios. Do not treat them as universal forecasts; retain in fact-review pending underlying evidence.
- The source's 30% EV-share goal also needs its policy scope verified.

topics.title: Tamu Lhosar
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Identification
- **Gurung community**, predominantly Nepal: New Year celebration; **Tamu** refers to Gurung people and **Lhosar** to New Year.
- Observed on **15 Poush** (late December); festivities include feasts, dances, music and ethnic dress.
- Associated districts: Lamjung, Gorkha, Tanahun, Syangja, Manang, Kaski and Parbat; Kathmandu's Tundikhel hosts celebrations, but the festival is not exclusive to the capital.
- Source dress terms: women - Makhamali blouse/Ghalek shawl; men - Bhoto/Bhangra/Kachhad.
## Significance and exam trap
- Cultural continuity, community identity, intergenerational transmission and tourism; Nepal recognises the festival as a holiday.
- **Do not equate 15 Poush with the astronomical winter solstice.** The supplied practice question incorrectly treats the solstice claim as true.

topics.title: Manufacturing, Make in India and PLI
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Policy framework
- **Make in India (2014)**: investment, manufacturing capability and employment.
- **PLI (introduced 2020)**: incentives linked to eligible incremental production/sales; coverage expanded across **14 sectors**. Defence and toys are not automatically PLI-covered merely because domestic manufacturing is promoted.
- Supporting levers: industrial corridors, logistics parks, National Infrastructure Pipeline, skills, infrastructure and business reforms.
## January 2025 source claims
- PDFs report Rs 1.28 lakh crore investment and 8.5 lakh jobs, mobile-phone production +600% and toy exports +239%; the measurement windows are unspecified, so use only after baseline verification.
## Opportunities and constraints
- Electronics, pharmaceuticals, renewable-energy equipment and defence; supply-chain diversification after COVID-19 can attract investment.
- Challenges: logistics, skills, technology, predictable regulation, environmental compliance and competition from Vietnam/Bangladesh.
- **India did not join RCEP in November 2019.** The source's claim that RCEP participation strengthened India's manufacturing position is wrong. [Commerce Ministry/PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=200213).
## Mains approach
- Combine productivity and scale with jobs, domestic supplier capacity, resilient trade links and sustainable production.
## Specialty steel: PLI 1.1
- Launched **6 January 2025**, second round; production period **FY 2025–26 to 2029–30**. First specialty-steel round notified **29 July 2021**, within the broader PLI initiative begun in 2020.
- Five categories: **coated/plated steel; high-strength/wear-resistant steel; specialty rails; alloy steel and wires; electrical steel**. Uses: automobiles, white goods, transformers and specialised industries.
- Changes: lower **CRGO** investment/capacity thresholds; excess production carried forward to the **immediately following year** for incentive eligibility; augmentation of existing mills eligible; quality/energy efficiency/process improvement.
- **Cold-Rolled Grain-Oriented steel**: transformer cores, high-tension power distribution; January 2025 ministry says domestic technology gap. Do not treat this as a timeless 'no Indian producer' claim.
- **PLI rewards eligible production, not simply any steel investment**. [Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2090683&lang=2&reg=48).

## Andhra Pradesh project map: January 2025
- Projects announced/inaugurated/foundation stones at Visakhapatnam worth **over ₹2 lakh crore** include clean energy, railways and manufacturing; not all are completed factories.
- **South Coast Railway headquarters, Visakhapatnam**: regional rail administration/connectivity.
- **Bulk Drug Park, Nakkapalli, Anakapalli district**, near **Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor**; APIs/pharmaceutical supply chains and reduced import dependence.
- **Krishnapatnam Industrial Area / KRIS City**, **Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor**; source **₹10,500 crore**, potential **~1 lakh jobs**; greenfield smart industrial development under **National Industrial Corridor Development Programme**.
- Evaluate land/clearance, water/power, logistics, skills, local benefits and ecological compliance; expected jobs are projections.

topics.title: Defence manufacturing and exports
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Dated figures and targets
- FY2023-24 exports: **Rs 21,083 crore**, source reports **32.5% annual growth**, private sector 60% / DPSUs 40%.
- FY2024-25 defence allocation reported: **Rs 6.22 lakh crore**. Source production figures: Rs 74,054 crore (2016-17) to Rs 108,684 crore (2022-23), with 21.96% private share in the latter year.
- Export ambition: **Rs 50,000 crore by 2028-29/2029**. Keep a target separate from an achieved outcome.
- CareEdge forecast cited: sector growth 20% CAGR and exports 19% CAGR over FY24-FY29; these are projections, not observed growth.
## Drivers and constraints
- Indigenisation, procurement demand, export facilitation, technology transfer and startups; benefits include strategic autonomy, employment and technology spillovers.
- Constraints: critical subsystem/design gaps, R&D and finance, coordination, certification, long procurement cycles and dependence on imported technologies.
## Policy and strategy
- FDI: source cites 74% automatic route and up to 100% government route subject to applicable conditions; defence corridors in **UP and Tamil Nadu**; Strategic Partnership Model and export-promotion support.
- Do not memorise the source's defence **TUFS** claim without verification: TUFS is associated with textiles. The alleged 60% import share/startup count also lacks a clear baseline.
- Modern warfare requires cyber/AI/space skills, joint-service training and multi-domain readiness; defence attachés support military diplomacy. **Army War College: Mhow.**
## Mains answer plan
- Security need → domestic capability and exports → technology/finance gaps → predictable procurement, R&D, supplier development and jointness.
## Aero-engines: January 2025 development debate
- DRDO chief **Samir V. Kamat** called for foreign co-development of advanced engines; source describes demonstrated fourth-generation engine technologies and a future **sixth-generation ambition**, not an operational Indian sixth-generation engine.
- Desired **thrust-to-weight ratio above 10**, high-temperature **single-crystal turbine blades**, **powder-metallurgy discs**, **ceramic-matrix composites**; lighter, heat-resistant components improve efficiency/performance.
- Engine 'generation' terminology is not a universal substitute for fighter-aircraft generation; materials demonstrated are not proof a complete certified engine is ready.
- Test/manufacturing gaps: **high-altitude facility, flying test bed, large forging capacity**, source **50,000-tonne press**, skilled workforce and certification.
- Source investment proposal **₹40,000–50,000 crore**, approximate **$4–5 billion**; research share **5% → suggested 15% of defence budget** is an argument, not a notified requirement. Unspecified cross-country R&D percentages are not comparable verified series.
- **Safran (France), Rolls-Royce (UK), GE (USA)** cited as potential partners; discussion does not mean all proposed contracts signed.
- Benefits: autonomy, potential exports/jobs and spillovers to civil aviation, space and materials. Risks: IP/technology-transfer restrictions, dependence, delays and cost. Evaluate actual design access, domestic capability and certification milestones.

## HimKavach: cold-weather protection, January 2025
- DRDO **modular multi-layer clothing system**, reported to have cleared user trials; designed temperature range **+20°C to −60°C**, rugged/all-weather operation.
- Add/remove insulating layers; breathability and moisture management maintain comfort. Passive insulation **retains body heat**, not proof the clothing actively generates warmth.
- Earlier **ECWCS**, Extreme Cold Weather Clothing System, associated with **DIPAS**, three-layer protection; source's blanket claim it fails in all Siachen conditions is overstated.
- Trials/design range are not a guarantee of zero cold injury or proof universal troop rollout; exposure, fit, activity, shelter and acclimatisation still matter.

topics.title: Citizenship, visas and deportation
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Constitutional and statutory distinction
- **Part II, Articles 5-11** addresses citizenship at commencement and Parliament's power to legislate; it does not itself prescribe all present-day acquisition procedures.
- **Citizenship Act, 1955** governs birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory; loss through renunciation, termination or deprivation.
- Citizenship is a Union subject; **CAA 2019** provides a special route for specified Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan entering by **31 December 2014**, subject to statutory conditions/exemptions. It is not automatic citizenship for every such entrant.
## MHA annual report 2023-24: source figures
- FRRO deportations **2,331**: Nigeria 1,470; Bangladesh 411; Uganda 78; reasons include visa violations/overstay.
- **1,112** long-term visas to Pakistani minority-community members; LTV is not citizenship.
- Citizenship certificates **1,699**: registration **1,278** + naturalisation **421**; this source table excludes CAA figures.
- Foreign visitors **98 lakh**: Bangladesh 21.1 lakh, US 17.4 lakh, UK 9.9 lakh.
- Source lists Amendment Act years 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019; avoid turning this source list into an assertion that no other changes exist.
## NRI, PIO and OCI: diaspora distinction
| Term | Citizenship / meaning |
| --- | --- |
| NRI | Indian citizen residing abroad; residence definitions depend on the law/context |
| PIO | Person of Indian origin; historical/demographic description can continue |
| OCI cardholder | Eligible **foreign national**, registered under Citizenship Act, 1955 **section 7A**; not an Indian citizen |
- **PIO card scheme merged into OCI in 2015**; the demographic category 'person of Indian origin' was not abolished.
- Eligibility connects to qualifying Indian citizenship/territory and descendants, subject to statutory conditions; Pakistan/Bangladesh citizenship/ancestry exclusions apply as prescribed. Do not infer eligibility from Indian ethnicity alone.
- OCI is **not dual citizenship**. No Indian voting rights, election eligibility or ordinary entitlement to constitutional/public posts; visa/residence privileges and permitted activities remain subject to rules. [MHA explanation](https://www.mha.gov.in/PDF_Other/1OCIcardholder_Introduction_15112019.pdf), [OCI FAQ](https://ociservices.gov.in/onlineOCI/onlineOCI/faq).

topics.title: Similipal and tiger conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Similipal
- **Mayurbhanj, Odisha**; associated elephant-reserve landscape includes Hadgarh and Kuldiha sanctuaries. Named for red silk-cotton trees.
- Forests: moist mixed deciduous, semi-evergreen and dry deciduous with grasslands; rivers **Khairi and Deo**; elephants, carnivores and mugger crocodiles.
- UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves since **2009**; notable wild **pseudo-melanistic tigers**. Avoid the source's unsupported 'Asia's second-largest biosphere' ranking and any confusion between biosphere reserve, national park and tiger-reserve boundaries.
## Tiger basics
- National animal; **keystone/predator** and ecosystem-health indicator; IUCN **Endangered**, CITES **Appendix I**.
- **Project Tiger: 1973**; **NTCA** statutory authority; **M-STrIPES** supports monitoring/patrolling.
- 2022 All India Tiger Estimation: estimated **3,682**, range **3,167-3,925**. The source uses 3,167 without explaining that it is the lower bound. [Official estimate](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2076921&lang=1&reg=3).
- Source highlights MP, Karnataka, Uttarakhand; Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam landscape in AP/Telangana; Sundarbans mangrove tigers; Corbett reserve. Rankings require a stated metric/year.
- International cooperation: **Global Tiger Forum**; **TX2** goal sought to double wild tiger numbers by 2022.

topics.title: IN-SPACe, POEM and SpaDeX
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Institutions and platform
- **IN-SPACe**, under Department of Space: promotes, authorises and facilitates non-government space activities and access to infrastructure.
- **POEM** repurposes PSLV's spent fourth stage (**PS4**) into an orbital experimental platform: cheaper microgravity testing and space qualification without each experiment needing a full satellite.
## Mission facts
- **PSLV-C60/SpaDeX launched 30 December 2024**, not 18 December 2023 as printed in the source. [ISRO mission summary](https://new1.isro.gov.in/Atomospheric_Re_entry_of_POEM4.html).
- **POEM-4 carried 24 payloads: 14 ISRO/DoS + 10 non-government**, including academia/startups through IN-SPACe. SpaDeX satellites and hosted POEM payloads serve distinct experimental purposes. [ISRO payload details](https://www.isro.gov.in/POEM_4_Payloads_spadex.html).
## Mains significance
- Lower entry costs, private innovation, jobs, public-private collaboration, technology validation and downstream communication/navigation/science services.
- Needs: authorisation clarity, affordable infrastructure, safety/debris management, finance and competitive technology. Private participation does not mean privatisation of ISRO.
## POEM-4: plants and walking robotics
- **CROPS — Compact Research Module for Orbital Plant Studies**: cowpea germination under microgravity, reported within **four days**; automated thermal/environment control and a two-leaf-stage objective. A germination experiment does not yet establish a complete sustainable food system. [ISRO CROPS](https://www.isro.gov.in/CROPS.html).
- **RRM-TD — Relocatable Robotic Manipulator–Technology Demonstrator**, developed by **IISU**: **seven degrees of freedom**; relocates itself to defined targets using **inchworm walking**, rather than simply relocating objects. Potential: inspection, assembly and servicing. [ISRO payload description](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/POEM_4_Payloads_spadex.html).

topics.title: Former prime ministers: state funerals and memorials
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## December 2024 context
- Manmohan Singh died **26 December 2024**; seven-day mourning and a state funeral; cremated at **Nigambodh Ghat on 28 December**.
- Source account distinguishes state-funeral guidelines from **the absence of a specific rule mandating a memorial for every former PM**. Past commemorative practice is not itself a constitutional entitlement.
- MHA subsequently conveyed a commitment to allocate memorial space; retain this as the source's December 2024 account, not a claim about today's allocation status.
## Memorial associations
- Nehru - **Shanti Van**; Shastri - **Vijay Ghat**; Charan Singh - **Kisan Ghat**; Indira Gandhi - **Shakti Sthal**; Rajiv Gandhi - **Vir Bhumi**; P.V. Narasimha Rao - **Ekta Sthal**; Vajpayee - **Sadaiv Atal** at Smriti Sthal.
- Source notes exceptions/local sites, including V.P. Singh and Morarji Desai's Ahmedabad samadhi. Avoid its inconsistent assertion that every memorial is in/near Delhi.
- Upkeep depends on the site and responsible government/trust; source reports Vajpayee's memorial funded by Atal Smriti Nyas, Rs 10.51 crore.
## Governance link
- Clear, consistent criteria, transparent allocation and preservation of public commemorative spaces.

topics.title: Core industries and industrial indicators
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Eight core industries
- **Coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, electricity.**
- Index of Eight Core Industries (**ICI**) is a weighted output index; monthly release by **Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT**. The source series uses **2011-12** as base year.
## Source-series weights (%)
| Industry | Weight |
| --- | ---: |
| Refinery products | 28.04 |
| Electricity | 19.85 |
| Steel | 17.92 |
| Coal | 10.33 |
| Crude oil | 8.98 |
| Natural gas | 6.88 |
| Cement | 5.37 |
| Fertilisers | 2.63 |
## How to use
- Measure sector output relative to the base period; weights represent the constituent sectors within the index, not each sector's share of the entire economy.
- Infrastructure and manufacturing are linked through steel/cement, fuel and power; changes have downstream effects on construction, transport and finance.
- Published near month-end for the previous month's output, before that month's IIP release; distinguish growth rate from index level.
## Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI)
- Monthly business survey compiled by **S&P Global**, with manufacturing, services and composite measures. It is a **diffusion index**, not a GDP growth percentage.
- **Above 50 = expansion; 50 = no change; below 50 = contraction**, relative to the previous month. A fall from 56 to 53 means slower expansion, **not contraction** as the source incorrectly states. [S&P Global explanation](https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/solutions/products/pmi).
- Inputs include output, new orders, employment, delivery times and inventories; PMI gives an early signal before official output/GDP releases.
- **PMI vs IIP:** survey-based change in business conditions vs measured industrial output; services PMI is outside industrial-output coverage. Neither single reading mechanically determines RBI interest rates.

topics.title: Green steel and industrial decarbonisation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Policy status in December 2024
- Ministry of Steel was **preparing** a Green Steel Mission with estimated cost **Rs 15,000 crore**. The January PDF overstates this as an already implemented investment.
- Proposed elements: green-steel PLI, renewable-energy incentives and public procurement. Green-steel taxonomy released **12 December 2024**; decarbonisation roadmap drew on **14 task forces**. [Ministry review](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2088827&lang=2&reg=48).
## Transition levers
- Renewable electricity + energy efficiency; scrap recycling; hydrogen-based **direct reduced iron (DRI)**; carbon capture where technically/economically suitable.
- Related policies: National Steel Policy 2017 (300 Mt capacity ambition for 2030-31), Steel Scrap Recycling Policy 2019, Vehicle Scrapping Policy 2021 and National Green Hydrogen Mission.
## Dated industry context and trade-offs
- Source reports **139.15 Mt finished-steel production in 2023-24**; distinguish finished-steel output from crude-steel production/capacity.
- Gains: lower emissions/pollution, export competitiveness and green skills. Barriers: costly capital/hydrogen, reliable clean power, technology scale-up and financing for smaller producers.
- Way forward: R&D, pilots, standards, demand creation, PPPs and international technology/finance cooperation; align expansion with net-zero **2070**.

topics.title: Landslides and disaster relief
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Wayanad context
- January 2025 source discusses the 2024 Wayanad landslide and the Centre's assessment as a disaster of **severe nature**. It reports 254 deaths and 128 missing; these are reporting-time figures, not final totals.
- Impacts: displacement/trauma, infrastructure and crop losses, livelihood disruption, erosion and ecosystem damage; vulnerable groups need targeted assistance.
## Relief framework
- **Disaster Management Act, 2005**; NDMA for national disaster-policy coordination; SDRF provides state-level immediate relief.
- NDRF may supplement SDRF after assessment and prescribed procedure for severe disasters. **NCCF is the predecessor of NDRF**, not a separate contemporary additional fund as the source suggests. [Official fund explanation](https://ies.gov.in/arthapedia/concept/national-disaster-response-fund-ndrf).
- **NDRF fund ≠ National Disaster Response Force**; use full names to avoid confusion. Relief assistance is not full compensation for every loss.
## Risk reduction
- Hazard mapping, slope-sensitive land use and drainage, resilient roads/buildings, local rainfall monitoring and evacuation protocols; livelihood recovery and psychosocial support.
- Link to **Sendai Framework** and climate adaptation. A tsunami-warning system is a different hazard-specific example, not a landslide detector.
## Himalayan landslide dams
- Alaknanda study discussed on 9 January 2025: landslide blockage → temporary lake → possible dam breach → downstream flood. Risk combines slope failure with flood exposure; monitoring must follow both hazards.

topics.title: Sea otters and trophic cascades
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identification and ecological role
- **Enhydra lutris**, coastal North Pacific marine mammal, renowned for dense fur and tool use to open shellfish.
- **Keystone predator**: controls sea urchins and helps protect kelp; diet also includes crabs and other invertebrates. Source reports food intake up to 25% of body mass daily.
- California's **Elkhorn Slough** example: otter predation may help control invasive **European green crabs**, which damage native coastal habitats.
## Conservation
- Source lists IUCN **Endangered**; threats include oil spills, pollution, disease, prey/habitat change and climate impacts. Protect habitats, reduce pollution and monitor populations.
- Avoid the source's absolute 'smallest marine mammal' superlative; distinguish sea otters from freshwater/river otters.
## Recall chain
Sea otter predation → fewer grazing sea urchins → healthier kelp habitat → more biodiversity.

topics.title: Sevdalinka and intangible cultural heritage
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Prelims identification
- **Bosnia and Herzegovina**; traditional urban folk singing, sometimes called Balkan blues.
- Blends South-Slavic oral poetry and Ottoman musical influences; storytelling, often love/longing; performed a cappella or with instruments.
- Inscribed in **2024 on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**. The source's phrase 'UNESCO National Inventory' conflates a national inventory with the international list. [UNESCO inscription](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/sevdalinka-traditional-urban-folk-song-01872).
## Heritage framework
- UNESCO **2003 Convention**: safeguarding living practices, expressions and transmitted knowledge; distinct from tangible monuments.
- Transmission: families, imitation, lessons, workshops and institutions. Supports identity, inclusion and intercommunity ties; safeguarding should keep practice alive rather than freeze it.

topics.title: Vasilopita
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Identification
- **Greek New Year cake/bread**, linked to **Saint Basil the Great**, a fourth-century bishop associated with charity.
- A hidden coin (**flouri**) signifies good fortune for the recipient; family/community sharing expresses faith, charity and togetherness.
- Source describes symbolic first slices for Christ, Virgin Mary and Saint Basil; practices can vary by household.
## UPSC link
- Match tradition with Greece/Greek Orthodox culture; use as an example of living heritage and community solidarity, not as a universal ritual followed identically everywhere.

topics.title: Thiruvalluvar, Thirukkural and Kanyakumari
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Thirukkural
- Tamil poet-philosopher **Thiruvalluvar**; dates remain debated, so no unsupported birth/reign year.
- **1,330 couplets = 133 chapters × 10 couplets**.
- Three divisions: **Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth/statecraft), Inbam (love)**; ethical themes include honesty, compassion, moderation, justice and public welfare.
- Sites: Thiruvalluvar statue at Kanyakumari; **Valluvar Kottam, Chennai**.
## December 2024 news
- Source reports glass bridge inaugurated **31 December 2024**, joining **Vivekananda Rock Memorial and Thiruvalluvar statue**, length 77 m, width 10 m, cost about Rs 37 crore; Thirukkural Week proposed for the last week of December.
- **Do not memorise the source's 133-foot bridge height**: it appears to confuse the statue's height with the bridge. Global 'longest/highest' rankings are also unverified.
## Mains use
- Heritage-linked tourism can support crafts/jobs; plan for marine ecology, coastal weather, maintenance and accessible/safe visitor movement. Ethics examples: wealth for social welfare and responsible governance.

topics.title: Carnatic music and Sangita Kalanidhi
topics.subject: Indian Art and Culture
topics.markdown:
## Music fundamentals
- South Indian classical tradition: **raga** (melodic framework), **tala** (rhythmic cycle), composed repertoire and substantial improvisation.
- Common languages: Telugu, Sanskrit, Tamil, Kannada; instruments: veena, violin, mridangam, flute. Bhakti traditions strongly influenced devotional repertoire.
- Examples: M.S. Subbulakshmi, Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer; Chennai's December/Margazhi season supports performance and transmission.
- **Do not read composition-centred as absence of improvisation.** Avoid rigid religious/cultural binaries with Hindustani music.
## Institution and award
- Music Academy arose from the **1927 Madras Congress/music conference** and was inaugurated **18 August 1928**; annual conferences began 1929. [Academy history](https://musicacademymadras.in/history/).
- **Sangita Kalanidhi title instituted 1942**, awarded by the Music Academy, Madras; gold medal and **birudu patra** (citation). Earlier conference presidents appear retrospectively in the recipient list. [Award history](https://musicacademymadras.in/sangita-kalanidhi/).

topics.title: Vaghsheer, Surat and Nilgiri
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Match the platform
| Platform | Project/class | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| INS Vaghsheer | Project 75 / Kalvari (Scorpene) | Sixth/final diesel-electric submarine |
| INS Surat | Project 15B | Fourth/final stealth destroyer |
| INS Nilgiri | Project 17A | Lead stealth frigate |
- Built at **Mazagon Dock, Mumbai**; Scorpene construction involves France's **Naval Group**.
- January 2 source anticipated commissioning on January 15. **All three were commissioned 15 January 2025**. [Official commissioning](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2092999&lang=2&reg=48).
## Capabilities and distinctions
- Vaghsheer: acoustic stealth, torpedoes, anti-ship missiles, sonar; anti-surface/submarine warfare, intelligence and surveillance. It is **conventionally powered**, not a nuclear ballistic-missile deterrent submarine.
- Surat strengthens surface/air defence; Nilgiri adds multipurpose stealth and anti-submarine capability.
- Significance: Indian Ocean security, fleet modernisation, indigenous shipbuilding, technology transfer and domestic supplier skills. Do not assume all design/IP is indigenous merely because construction occurs in India.
- The 6 January source again mentions Vaghsheer, but misprints its commissioning year as 2024; the verified date remains **15 January 2025**.

topics.title: Delimitation, fertility and federal representation
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 editorial argument
- Southern states fear reduced relative parliamentary representation after population-based delimitation because fertility fell earlier than in many northern states.
- The article discusses Andhra Pradesh reversing a two-child electoral restriction and proposals for larger families. These are reported political responses, not settled national policy.
- **Pro-natal incentives may not reverse low fertility effectively**; China, Japan and South Korea illustrate limits of coercion or incentives and the importance of population composition, ageing and dependency.
- A simple headcount can overlook achievements in education, health and demographic transition; representation must reconcile voter equality and federal fairness.
## Gender and policy dimensions
- Childbearing involves lost earnings, unpaid care and constraints on women's autonomy; childcare, social protection and compensation/support are more substantive than appeals to reproduce.
- Migration can address regional labour/population imbalances sooner than fertility changes; it does not by itself settle constitutional seat allocation.
## Mains distinction
- **Author's proposal:** revisit purely count-based representation and consider broader capability characteristics.
- This is an editorial position, not an enacted delimitation formula. Assess alternatives against constitutional equality, federalism, feasibility and women's reproductive choice.

topics.title: Manmohan Singh and economic liberalisation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Career and reform context
- Finance Minister **1991-96**, Prime Minister **2004-14**; Cambridge economics Tripos **1957**, Oxford DPhil **1962**; earlier RBI Governor and Planning Commission Deputy Chairman.
- **1991 balance-of-payments crisis** triggered stabilisation and structural reform: rupee devaluation, fiscal discipline, lower trade barriers, industrial delicensing and greater scope for private/foreign investment. These were government-wide reforms, not the actions of one office alone.
## Economic approach
- Markets with an enabling state; inclusive growth rather than indiscriminate punitive redistribution; exports and global integration; autonomy/accountability for PSUs.
- Human capital: education, health, women's literacy, nutrition and sanitation support productivity and opportunity.
## Effects and debate
- Greater competition, FDI and integration helped services/IT expansion and later growth. Remaining concerns: unequal gains, implementation/institutional capacity, infrastructure and governance.
- Coalition-era criticism included corruption allegations and policy paralysis; **allegations are not findings of personal guilt**.
- Source claims second-term growth averaged over 8% without a series/period; do not memorise this unsupported average.
## Mains plan
- Crisis → stabilisation measures → industrial/trade/financial reforms → growth and integration → inequality, governance and institution-building challenges.
## Embedded editorial: growth, work and welfare
- Santosh Mehrotra's retrospective highlights five channels: higher savings/investment, non-farm jobs, rising real wages, rural employment support and poverty reduction.
- Editorial figures: savings/investment around **23%/24% of GDP in 2003-04**, rising towards **35%/38%**; average growth **7.8% during 2004-14**. These do not establish the PDF's separate 'over 8% in the second term' claim.
- Jobs narrative: about **7.5 million non-farm jobs annually**; construction jobs **26 million (2004) → 54 million (2012)**; manufacturing **52 → 60 million**; agricultural employment fell by about **6.7 crore between 2004-05 and 2017-18**.
- **MGNREGA Act, 2005** provided an employer-of-last-resort channel; source links wages and private consumption to poverty decline **138 million fewer poor during 2004-05 to 2011-12**.
- Article contrasts later conditions: annual non-farm job additions **7.5 million (2004-13) → 2.9 million (2013-19)**; youth unemployment **6% (2011-12) → 12% (2022-23)**; graduate unemployment about **29%**, postgraduate **33%**. These are the author's figures with varying datasets/periods, not one harmonised series.
- Manufacturing's GVA share reportedly reached **17%** earlier and fell to **13% in 2022**; manufacturing jobs **60 million (2012), 56 million (2019), 62.9 million (2022)**. Merchandise exports: **$77 billion (2004), $323 billion (2014), $454 billion (2024)**.
- Unpaid-family-work concern: share **23.8% (2012), 20.9% (2019), 20.2% (2024)**; counts **111 million (2004), 85.8 million (2012), 107.8 million (2018), 104 million (2023)**. Include unpaid work when judging labour quality; rising employment alone does not establish decent work.
- The author's criticism of demonetisation, GST implementation and COVID lockdown concerns informal-sector disruption; evaluate evidence and causal claims rather than memorise opinion as settled fact.
## Ethics illustration
- A companion memoir portrays courteous leadership, humour, humility, tolerance of uncomfortable press questions and delegation to capable colleagues. Use as a qualitative example, not as a measurable policy outcome.

topics.title: Injectable hydrogel for targeted cancer therapy
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Research mechanism
- **IIT Guwahati + Bose Institute, Kolkata**: ultra-short peptide hydrogel for local delivery of chemotherapy, reported **2 January 2025**.
- Hydrogel: water-rich three-dimensional polymer/peptide network; a local drug reservoir that responds to elevated **glutathione (GSH)** at the tumour site.
- Experimental work used **doxorubicin** in a **murine breast-cancer model**. This is preclinical research, not an approved human cure. [IIT Guwahati](https://www.iitg.ac.in/iitg_press_details?p=158%2Fiit-guwahati-researchers-develop-innovative-injectable-hydrogel-for-targeted-breast-cancer-therapy), [Research abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39552584/).
## Why it matters
- Local/sustained drug release may reduce systemic exposure and improve delivery; the source's assertion that only tumour cells are affected is too absolute.
- Translation needs safety, biocompatibility, dose/release control, clinical trials, scalable manufacture and affordability; lower resistance/cost are potential benefits, not established clinical outcomes.

topics.title: Credit ratings and rating agencies
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Meaning and regulator
- Assessment of a borrower's/debt instrument's creditworthiness and ability to pay principal/interest; applies to corporates, governments and specified debt instruments.
- India's securities credit-rating agencies are regulated by **SEBI under the CRA Regulations, 1999**, not RBI. [SEBI regulations listing](https://sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?cid=21&doListingAll=yes).
- Global examples: **S&P, Moody's, Fitch**. Source's 95% market-share claim needs a dated market definition.
- Source list includes CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, SMERA/Acuité, Fitch India/India Ratings and Brickwork; avoid a fixed 'six agencies' assertion or outdated names without checking the applicable registry/date.
## PYQ distinction
- **ICRA is a public limited company; Brickwork Ratings is an Indian agency.** UPSC Prelims 2022 answer **(b), 2 and 3 only**; preserve the exam's historical statements rather than infer today's licence status.
- Ratings express credit-risk opinions; they are not guarantees against default and are different from a borrower's personal credit score.

topics.title: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV)
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Virus and disease
- Respiratory virus identified **2001**, causing upper/lower respiratory infections; clinically resembles RSV and other respiratory illnesses.
- Symptoms: cough, fever, nasal congestion, wheeze or shortness of breath; severe disease can include bronchiolitis/pneumonia. Higher risk: young children, older adults and immunocompromised people.
- Spread: respiratory secretions, close contact and contaminated surfaces; usual incubation **3-6 days**. Late-winter/spring circulation is documented in temperate US settings, not a universal calendar for every country.
- **No specific antiviral treatment or vaccine**; care is supportive. Hand hygiene, covering coughs and staying away from others while ill help reduce spread. [CDC overview](https://www.cdc.gov/human-metapneumovirus/about/).
## January 2025 context
- Source discusses increased respiratory infections in China; hospital videos/social-media claims do not establish a new pandemic. Distinguish surveillance evidence from rumours and HMPV from a newly discovered pathogen.
- Co-circulating pathogens mentioned: influenza A, SARS-CoV-2 and **Mycoplasma pneumoniae (a bacterium, not a virus)**.
- Cover confirms **4 January 2025**; the inner heading incorrectly says January 2024.
## January 7 consolidation
- The source again reports cough, fever, nasal congestion, wheezing and breathing difficulty; severe disease can involve **bronchiolitis, bronchitis or pneumonia**, especially children, older adults, immunocompromised people and people with chronic lung disease.
- HMPV circulates seasonally, often winter/spring in temperate regions; outbreaks do not establish a novel virus or pandemic. Do not use social-media hospital/cemetery claims as epidemiological evidence.
- Source '2–5 days of illness' is not a guaranteed duration; severity and underlying health vary. **Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a bacterium**, despite its placement in the PDF's 'other viruses' list.

topics.title: Banana cultivation and exports
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Cultivation
- Tropical crop; source growing conditions: **15-35°C**, relative humidity **75-85%**, deep fertile well-drained loam and pH **6.5-7.5**. Suitability varies by cultivar/local conditions.
- Varieties: **Dwarf Cavendish, Robusta, Monthan, Poovan, Nendran**.
- Major producing states named: **Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat**.
## Export context
- Source attributes to **APEDA** a tenfold export increase over the preceding decade and **$1 billion ambition over the next five years**; this is a January 2025 reported target, not achieved exports.
- Supply-chain focus: quality, handling, cold-chain/transport, reliable markets and farmer value realisation.

topics.title: Non-performing assets (NPAs)
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Definition and ratios
- Broadly, a bank loan is NPA when interest/principal is overdue **more than 90 days**; RBI rules contain category-specific criteria, including crop-season treatment for eligible agricultural advances.
- **Gross NPA**: all assets classified as non-performing before relevant deductions; **GNPA ratio** relates gross NPAs to gross advances.
- December 2024 Financial Stability Report: source reports scheduled-commercial-bank GNPA ratio **2.6%, a 12-year low**. Keep this historical observation separate from later reports/projections.
## Interpretation
- Lower ratio may reflect recoveries, lower fresh slippages, write-offs and loan growth. A write-off is not the same as recovery or automatic debt forgiveness.
- Mains: underwriting/monitoring, resolution/recovery, capital adequacy and macroeconomic risks; don't apply the 90-day shorthand without recognising special RBI classifications.

topics.title: Norovirus
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Identification and spread
- Highly contagious virus causing **acute gastroenteritis**: vomiting, diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal discomfort. 'Stomach flu' does **not** mean influenza.
- Faecal-oral transmission through contaminated food/water, surfaces and close contact; outbreaks can spread rapidly in shared settings.
- Supportive care/rehydration is central; no specific antiviral medicine. Antibiotics do not treat a viral infection.
- Source reports environmental persistence, including freezing and heat exposure near 60°C; do not use that as a food-safety or disinfection instruction.
## Prevention and context
- Soap-and-water handwashing, safe food handling, effective environmental cleaning and keeping symptomatic handlers away from food preparation.
- January source refers to a US case surge; it is a dated surveillance context, not a claim about current outbreak levels.

topics.title: Tobacco Board and FCV tobacco
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **Tobacco Board Act, 1975**; Board came into existence **1 January 1976**; headquarters **Guntur, Andhra Pradesh**.
- Under **Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry**; regulates/helps develop production, marketing and exports, especially **Flue-Cured Virginia (FCV)** tobacco. [Board's institutional history](https://tobaccoboard.commerce.gov.in/bactivities.php).
## January 2025 source context
- Reports FCV farmers' earnings more than doubled between **2019-20 and 2023-24**; tobacco-production rankings cited (India second after China, fourth in FCV) require the reference year's dataset.
- FCV is widely used in cigarettes; link crop/export economics with public-health externalities rather than treating income growth as the only outcome.

topics.title: National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG)
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Institutional map
- NMCG registered as a society in **2011** under the **Societies Registration Act, 1860**; functions under **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
- Earlier implementation arm of **National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA)**, constituted under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; replaced by **National Ganga Council in 2016**, chaired by the **Prime Minister**.
- Source describes Governing Council and Executive Committee, headed by NMCG Director General; objectives are pollution abatement, conservation and rejuvenation through a **river-basin approach**.
## January news and mains use
- Source highlights Chandauli sewage-treatment initiative. Sewage collection plus reliable plant operation, discharge monitoring and ecosystem-flow management matter more than capacity announcements alone.
- Link sanitation, river ecology, municipal capacity and basin-wide coordination.

topics.title: Simultaneous elections and federalism
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Proposal and constitutional questions
- Synchronise Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections; distinguish this from any separate plan for local-body elections. The January 2025 discussion is a **proposal**, not proof of enacted implementation.
- Relevant term provisions: **Article 83** (Parliament) and **Article 172** (State legislatures); synchronisation and premature dissolution raise tenure and accountability questions.
## Arguments to balance
- Benefits claimed: lower repeated election costs, less recurring deployment/model-code disruption and more sustained governance.
- Concerns: curtailed state mandates, national campaigns crowding out local issues, regional-party/federal autonomy, major logistical demand and short remaining terms after mid-cycle elections.
- The source's critical editorial stance is an argument, not a judicial finding that simultaneous elections are unconstitutional.
## Linked safeguards
- **Article 356**: President's Rule; **S.R. Bommai (1994)** limits arbitrary dismissal and recognises federalism. Source's 'first President's Rule in Kerala 1959' is incorrect; Punjab had an earlier imposition in 1951. [Parliamentary reference](https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/761237/1/Presidents_Rule_in_St_UT_Eng_9th_ed_2016.pdf).
- **Tenth Schedule, 52nd Amendment (1985)**: anti-defection; timely adjudication, Speaker neutrality and lawful merger provisions need attention. Do not confuse the surviving merger exception with the removed one-third split exemption.
## Mains conclusion
- Evaluate efficiency alongside federalism, meaningful electoral choice, constitutional procedure and government stability; recommend consensus, independent administration and credible mid-term safeguards.
## Historical cycle
- Lok Sabha/assembly elections broadly coincided in **1952, 1957, 1962, 1967**. Premature assembly dissolutions in **1968-69** and Lok Sabha dissolution in **1970**, followed by the **1971** election, disrupted synchronisation.

topics.title: Tungsten: properties, ores and uses
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Prelims facts
- Symbol **W**; melting point about **3,422°C**, highest among metals; used for hard, heat-resistant materials.
- Ores: **wolframite (Fe,Mn)WO4**, **scheelite CaWO4**, **ferberite FeWO4**; deposits often associated with hydrothermal processes.
- Applications: tungsten carbides/cutting tools, alloy/special steels, hard-facing materials, armour/ammunition components and historically bulb filaments; alloys may include chromium, nickel, molybdenum or titanium.
## Source resource figures
- Karnataka **42%**, Rajasthan **27%**, Andhra Pradesh **17%**, Maharashtra **9%**; remaining 5% across Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. The resource inventory year is missing, so these are source figures pending verification.
- Source describes domestic dependence on imports, including trade partners Singapore/US/UK; export destinations Germany, US, Israel, UK, Japan, Sweden. They are dated/unspecified trade lists, not permanent rankings.
## Avoid unsupported absolutes
- Do not memorise 'resistant to all acids' or '95% used by steel' as universal facts. Distinguish mineral resources, economically recoverable reserves and actual production.
- Atomic number **74**, atomic mass about **183.84**, density about **19.3 g/cm³**; these appear in the source graphic.

topics.title: Trinidad and Tobago
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Map recall
- Capital **Port of Spain**; island country in the **south-eastern West Indies**, near north-eastern Venezuela and north-western Guyana; member of **CARICOM**.
- **Northern Range** linked geologically to Venezuela's coastal ranges; highest point **Mount Aripo**.
- **Pitch Lake**, Trinidad: natural asphalt deposit; rivers **Ortoire and Caroni**.
- January 2025 source context: emergency declared amid violence; retain as a dated news trigger, not a permanent governance status.

## Diaspora link
- **January 2025**: President **Christine Carla Kangaloo** was chief guest of the 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas in Bhubaneswar, addressing virtually; an example of Indian Caribbean diaspora links.

topics.title: Quad and the Indo-Pacific
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Members and chronology
- **India, US, Japan, Australia**; an informal diplomatic grouping without a mutual-defence treaty.
- **2004** Indian Ocean tsunami: coordinated humanitarian relief; **2007** first Quad dialogue; stalled in **2008**; revived in **2017**.
- Foreign ministers marked **20 years of cooperation on 31 December 2024**. [Joint statement](https://www.foreignminister.gov.au/minister/penny-wong/media-release/joint-statement-quad-foreign-ministers-commemorating-20th-anniversary-quad-cooperation).
## Agenda: maritime security + public goods
| Initiative | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| IPMDA | Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness; maritime information, illegal fishing and security |
| MAITRI | Maritime Initiative for Training in the Indo-Pacific; operational skills and maritime law enforcement |
| Quad Cancer Moonshot | Initial focus on cervical cancer |
| Open RAN | Interoperable telecom architecture and resilient networks |
| Quad Fellowship | STEM education and research |
- Free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific; navigation, rules, ASEAN centrality, climate/disaster resilience, health and technology.
- **Malabar** is a naval exercise involving the four countries, with its own history; it is not the Quad's founding treaty.
## India: significance and limits
- Protect sea lanes, balance coercion, strengthen disaster response, build resilient supply chains and access technology/research cooperation.
- Challenges: different national priorities, uncertain resources, informal coordination, China-related tensions and overlap with other arrangements, including AUKUS.
- Better delivery: practical projects, predictable funding, ASEAN consultation and coordination. Membership expansion is an editorial suggestion, not an agreed decision.
## Prelims traps
- Do not call Quad a formal military alliance or a trade bloc merely because a Mains question uses that premise.
- The **Supply Chain Resilience Initiative** involves India, Japan and Australia; do not equate it automatically with a four-member Quad programme.
- The PDF conflates the 2007 dialogue with Abe's later 'security diamond' formulation; memorise the verified Quad chronology above.

topics.title: Groundwater quality and management
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Contaminants: cause → impact
| Contaminant | Main pathway | Recall |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nitrate | Fertiliser leaching, sewage/septic leakage, waste | Infant methemoglobinemia / blue-baby syndrome |
| Fluoride | Often natural rock-water interaction | Dental and skeletal fluorosis at excessive exposure |
| Uranium | Often geogenic; chemistry and abstraction matter | Kidney toxicity is a major concern |
| Other pollutants | Industry, landfills, hazardous storage | Metals, organic contaminants and salinity |
- Excess irrigation/abstraction can worsen transport or concentration; quality and quantity must be assessed together. Polluted irrigation water can affect soils, crops and food chains.
## January 2025 report: retain scope
- PDF reports nitrate exceedance in **440 districts in 2023**, compared with **359 in 2017**, and about **56% of districts** affected. District occurrence is not the percentage of unsafe wells.
- Source hotspot figures: **Rajasthan 49%, Karnataka 48%, Tamil Nadu 37%**; **30.77% pre-monsoon → 32.66% post-monsoon** exceedance. The supplied summary does not reliably define every denominator/sample universe; treat these as report-specific figures, not universal national rates.
- Fluoride hotspots listed: Rajasthan, Haryana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; uranium: Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
- Source extraction stage about **60.4%**, and 'safe' assessment units about **73%**, compared with **67.4% in 2022**. **Safe extraction status does not certify safe drinking-water quality.** [CGWB 2024 reports](https://www.cgwb.gov.in/en/node/2012).
## Threshold trap
- **BIS drinking-water nitrate limit: 45 mg/L. WHO guideline: 50 mg/L as nitrate ion**; specify the standard and chemical reporting basis.
- The PDF's practice answer wrongly treats the WHO 50 mg/L statement as false by substituting India's threshold. [WHO nitrate fact sheet](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/wash-documents/water-safety-and-quality/chemical-fact-sheets-2022/nitrate-and-nitrite-fact-sheet-2022.pdf).
## Institutions and programmes
- **CGWB**: scientific assessment, exploration, aquifer mapping, level/quality monitoring, recharge studies, reports, yearbooks, atlases and training; Ministry of Jal Shakti. Established in **1970** by renaming the Exploratory Tube Wells Organisation; merger with GSI's groundwater wing in **1972**.
- **CGWA**: groundwater extraction regulation under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; distinguish its regulatory role from CGWB's scientific work.
- **NAQUIM** maps and manages aquifers; **Atal Bhujal Yojana** promotes community groundwater management; **Jal Shakti Abhiyan / Catch the Rain** encourage conservation and recharge.
- CPCB/SPCB pollution control under the Water Act, 1974; sewage/effluent treatment prevents contamination at source.
## Mains response
- Monitor hotspots and disclose water quality → reduce fertiliser losses and repair sanitation → enforce industrial waste controls → provide safe alternative drinking water → recharge with quality safeguards.
- Combine metering/water budgets, efficient irrigation, community participation and demand management; recharge alone cannot offset unlimited extraction.
- Benefits: health protection, reliable food production, lower treatment costs and reduced ecological damage. Avoid recharge structures that inject contaminated runoff.

topics.title: Renewable energy and grid integration
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Target and January 2025 snapshot
- India's announced 2030 target is **500 GW installed electricity capacity from non-fossil sources**. Non-fossil includes nuclear; capacity is not electricity actually generated.
- Source **November 2024** snapshot: **158.55 GW renewable capacity excluding large hydro**; solar **94.17**, wind **47.95**, small hydro **5.08**, biomass **10.72**, waste-to-energy **0.61 GW**. Components differ slightly from the rounded total.
- Solar subdivisions reported: rooftop **15.16 GW**, off-grid **4.10 GW**. These are dated source figures, not current totals.
## Resources and sites
| Resource | Location / limitation |
| --- | --- |
| Solar | Strong potential in Rajasthan, Gujarat and other high-insolation regions; land and grid access matter |
| Wind | Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka; potential depends on hub height and methodology |
| Offshore wind | Gujarat and Tamil Nadu coasts; high capital and marine infrastructure needs |
| Hydro | Himalayan and other suitable basins; social/ecological impacts and seasonal flows |
| Geothermal | Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand examples in source |
| Ocean energy | Gulf of Kutch and Sundarbans cited for tidal prospects; wave/tidal technologies remain distinct |
- Source indicative potentials: solar **748 GW**, wind **over 300 GW**, hydro **148 GW**, geothermal **10 GW**, ocean **40 GW**; assumptions/dates differ. Do not compare them as equally deployable capacity.
- Source '46 GW hydro remains untapped' conflicts with its potential/installed-capacity discussion; do not memorise that classification without the original assessment.
## Deployment barriers → response
- Land fragmentation/community conflict → transparent land records, consent, compensation, agrivoltaics and other dual use.
- High upfront costs/uncertain revenues → predictable tariffs/contracts, affordable finance and research.
- Variable output/grid congestion/curtailment → stronger transmission, forecasting, flexible demand, storage and wind-solar hybrids.
- Saturation of good wind sites → suitable repowering/site assessment; offshore pilots where viable.
- Clearance/policy uncertainty → coordinated predictable rules without bypassing environmental assessment.
- Component waste/skills gaps → recycling, training and community engagement.
## Schemes and grid
- **PM-KUSUM**: decentralised solar generation, stand-alone pumps and solarisation of grid-connected pumps; farmer energy/income support.
- Solar-PV **PLI**, Solar Parks, National Bioenergy Programme and foreign investment support production/deployment.
- **Green Energy Corridor**: transmission links from renewable-rich regions to demand centres, plus grid integration. Storage and smart grids complement transmission; they are not substitutes for it.
- **Pradhan Mantri Suryodaya** concerned **rooftop solar**, not the PDF's claimed large-scale solar parks. **PM-Surya Ghar** was approved on **29 February 2024**, with **₹75,021 crore** and a one-crore-household aim. [Cabinet decision](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2010133&lang=2&reg=3).
- National Green Hydrogen Mission's 2030 expectations in the graphic: **5 MMT/year hydrogen**, about **125 GW associated renewable addition**, **₹8 lakh crore investment**, **6 lakh jobs**, **50 MMT/year CO₂ avoided**. These are mission projections, not achieved outcomes.
## Mains value
- Cleaner electricity can reduce import dependence, create jobs and improve access; benefits require reliable grids and affordable supply.
- Carbon-intensity reduction, non-fossil capacity share and renewable generation share are different indicators.
## Green hydrogen and Pudimadaka hub
- Renewable electricity → **water electrolysis** → hydrogen + oxygen; hydrogen may be stored/transported or converted into derivatives; a **fuel cell** converts hydrogen/oxygen into electricity and water. Electricity origin and lifecycle emissions distinguish green production from fossil-based hydrogen.
- **January 2025 foundation-stone stage**, **Pudimadaka near Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh**, **NTPC Green Energy Ltd**; first green-hydrogen hub under **National Green Hydrogen Mission**, planned **₹1.85 lakh crore** investment.
- Source focuses on **green methanol, green urea and sustainable aviation fuel**, exports and energy transition; construction announcements are not achieved output. [PMO project release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2090664&lang=2&reg=48).

## GEAPP, ISA and grid digitalisation: January 2025
- **Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet**: philanthropic, government, technology, policy and financing partners; clean-energy access, growth and climate goals.
- Source ambitions: avoid **4 gigatonnes future carbon emissions**, energy access for **1 billion people**, enable **150 million jobs**; targets, not achieved totals.
- **ISA Multi-Donor Trust Fund**, mobilisation goal **$100 million** for solar projects; GEAPP project-management support includes governance, fundraising, financing and implementation.
- **DUET = Digitalization of Utilities for Energy Transition**: digital grid-asset inventory with coordinates/specifications + live smart sensors → load-flow analysis and voltage/current/phase tracking → reduced transmission/distribution losses.
- **ENTICE = Energy Transitions Innovation Challenge**, first launched **2023**; **ENTICE 2.0** planned January 2025, scaling investable solutions through funding, markets and mentorship.
- Distinguish philanthropic partnership/trust fund from a treaty-created global climate-finance mechanism; neither pledges nor digitised assets alone prove delivered energy access.

topics.title: Vikram Sarabhai and institution building
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Timeline
| Year | Milestone |
| --- | --- |
| 1919, 12 August | Born in Ahmedabad |
| 1940 | Natural Sciences Tripos, Cambridge; later cosmic-ray research at IISc under C.V. Raman |
| 1947 | Cambridge PhD; Physical Research Laboratory, Ahmedabad |
| 1961 | Key role in IIM Ahmedabad |
| 1962 | INCOSPAR; Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award |
| 1966 | Community Science Centre; Padma Bhushan; AEC chair after Homi Bhabha |
| 1969 | ISRO established |
| 1971, 30 December | Death |
| 1972 | Padma Vibhushan, posthumous |
| 1975 | Aryabhata launch; SITE began after his death |
- January 2025 source incorrectly calls the recent anniversary the **52nd**; **30 December 2024 was the 53rd**. [ISRO biography](https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/sarabhaiformer.html).
## Applications, institutions and legacy
- Central idea: use advanced science for **communication, education, weather, agriculture and national development**, alongside scientific research.
- **SITE, 1975–76**: Satellite Instructional Television Experiment; NASA's ATS-6 supported rural educational broadcasting. Conceived during his leadership and implemented after his death.
- **Aryabhata**, India's first satellite, launched in **1975**, not 1980; distinguishes satellite development from launch-vehicle milestones.
- Legacy centres: **VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram**; **Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad**; contributions to **ECIL, Hyderabad**, and India's uranium/nuclear institutions including **UCIL, Jaduguda**. Later centres/institutional mergers should not all be described as personally founded before his death.
- Source also notes international roles: Physics Section, Indian Science Congress (**1962**); IAEA General Conference (**1970**); UN peaceful uses of atomic energy conference (**1971**).
- **Sarabhai crater** on the Moon; the source attributes 'Mahatma Gandhi of Indian Science' to A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
## Exam distinctions
- **ISRO: 1969; Aryabhata: 1975; SITE: 1975–76**.
- The PDF's claim that SITE laid the foundation for a later Krishi Darshan is chronologically doubtful: do not use that causal sequence without checking the programme's earlier history.
- **Mangalyaan = Mars Orbiter Mission**; India succeeded on its first Mars-orbit attempt, but was not the second space entity to reach Mars.
- **GL-10 = NASA's electric aircraft demonstrator**. Both related PYQs were confirmed in the saved official **2016** UPSC Prelims GS-I paper and added to the common subject JSON.
## Ethics / Mains illustration
- Institution building, curiosity, interdisciplinary teamwork and public-purpose science; link innovation to social needs rather than list awards alone.

topics.title: Moldova, Transnistria and energy security
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Map and conflict
- **Moldova**: landlocked Eastern Europe, **Romania west; Ukraine north/east/south**.
- **Transnistria**: breakaway territory mainly along the eastern/left bank of the **Dniester/Nistru**, bordering Ukraine; de facto administration does not equal internationally recognised independence.
- Proclaimed separatist republic in **1990**, not the PDF's 1991 claim; armed conflict and ceasefire in **1992**. Russia supports the region, but support is not recognition of statehood. [OSCE conflict history](https://moldova.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/4/3/42308.pdf).
## January 2025 energy shock
- Russian gas supplies to Transnistria stopped on **1 January 2025**, as Ukraine transit arrangements expired; heating and gas-fired electricity were disrupted.
- The Moldova-wide effect included loss of electricity previously supplied by the Transnistrian power plant, but **Moldova proper had diversified supplies**. On 1–2 January, government reported electricity needs met through domestic production and Romanian imports. [Moldovan government](https://gov.md/en/press-releases/russia-scales-regional-security-risks-halting-gas-supplies-transnistrian-region).
- Do not reduce the crisis to 'all Moldova still buys all gas from Russia'; separate gas, electricity, the two banks and the reporting date.
## Diplomacy and Mains links
- India–Moldova diplomatic relations began in **1992**; the PDF cites a newly opened Moldovan embassy in New Delhi as diversification of external ties.
- Multiple passports among residents do not establish internationally recognised 'Transnistrian nationality'.
- Analyse energy dependence, geopolitical coercion, sovereignty, de facto control and winter humanitarian risk; diversification, interconnections and contingency planning increase resilience.

topics.title: India–Indonesia cooperation
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 context
- The PDF anticipated President **Prabowo Subianto's** Republic Day visit and cooperation proposals. Keep prospective proposals separate from concluded agreements.
- India links Indonesia with **Act East**, maritime security and wider Indo-Pacific engagement; Indonesia is an important **ASEAN** partner.
## Defence and technology
- **BrahMos**: India–Russia joint-venture **supersonic cruise missile**; variants for land, sea and air. The source discusses an Indonesian purchase proposal, not proof of a signed export contract.
- Possible cooperation in **Su-30 maintenance/upgrades**, training, technology transfer, exercises and maritime security; costs, budgets and recipient priorities shape procurement.
- Sea-lane security and a stable regional balance provide cooperation incentives; avoid describing every initiative solely as anti-China alignment.
## Public services and economy
- Interest in digital public services: **payments, e-governance and inclusion**, with access/privacy/capacity safeguards.
- School-meal cooperation links nutrition, attendance and learning; India's midday-meal experience is a comparison, not proof of identical schemes.
- Trade/investment opportunities cited: minerals, pharmaceuticals, renewable energy, infrastructure and manufacturing; ASEAN connections support market access.
## Mains frame
- Cooperation can combine security, economic links and public-service knowledge while each country preserves strategic autonomy.
- Evaluate deliverable projects, affordability, skills/technology transfer and local needs; distinguish diplomatic intent, MoUs and implemented outcomes.

topics.title: Matrimonial laws: protection and due process
topics.subject: Social Problems In India
topics.markdown:
## Legal framework
- **Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961**: dowry-related offences; **Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005**: protection, residence, monetary and other remedies for domestic violence, including physical, sexual, verbal/emotional and economic abuse.
- Source uses **IPC 498A**, cruelty by husband/relatives. For the new framework, **BNS section 85** creates the offence and **86** defines cruelty; old cases may continue under the applicable earlier law. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/handle/123456789/20062?col=123456789%2F1362&view_type=search).
- Cognizable/non-bailable classification **does not require automatic arrest**. Arrest necessity and procedural safeguards remain distinct from the existence of an accusation.
## Cases and source corrections
- **Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar, 2014**, not 2017 as printed: no routine/automatic arrest; apply the statutory necessity checklist and judicial scrutiny. A later 2017 judgment cites the 2014 precedent. [Supreme Court](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/6593/6593_2017_Order_27-Jul-2017.pdf).
- **Law Commission Report 243, August 2012** considered section 498A and safeguards. Recommendations are not automatically enacted law. [Report](https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3ca0daec69b5adc880fb464895726dbdf/uploads/2022/08/2022081023.pdf).
- The PDF's 'arrest immediately on complaint' and 'no punishment for false allegations' are overbroad; do not learn them as legal rules.
## Balanced Mains argument
- Genuine abuse/dowry violence require accessible protection, prompt investigation, legal aid and safe support.
- Proven malicious complaints or indiscriminate implication can cause stigma, livelihood loss, family distress and wasted judicial resources; unsupported allegations of misuse can also discourage genuine victims.
- **Acquittal or a withdrawn complaint alone does not prove fabrication**; assess evidence, not gender stereotypes.
- Responses: trained investigators, reasoned arrest decisions, timely trials, judicial oversight, survivor support, counselling where safe and voluntary, and action on demonstrated deliberate falsehood under applicable law.
- Gender-neutral reform is a policy debate; do not present the PDF's recommendations as current enacted provisions or dilute protection for victims.

topics.title: Great Nicobar: development, ecology and tribal rights
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Project and map recall
- **Great Nicobar**, southern Nicobar Islands, Andaman and Nicobar UT; strategic proximity to Indian Ocean sea lanes and Southeast Asia.
- Core integrated project: **container transshipment terminal at Galathea Bay, international airport, township and power plant**. [Environmental-clearance project record](https://environmentclearance.nic.in/auth/FORM_A_PDF.aspx?cat_id=IA%2FAN%2FNCP%2F201159%2F2021).
- The January 2025 PDF reports a **₹72,000-crore** overall proposal and an additional **100-acre seafront** request for cruise/tourism infrastructure and possible ship breaking. Do not replace the main container terminal with a cruise terminal or assume every additional proposal is approved.
## Ecological and social stakes
- Rainforests, mangroves, reefs and seagrass provide habitat/coastal protection; construction, dredging, pollution and noise may disrupt these systems.
- **Leatherback turtle nesting; Nicobar megapode; dugong/seagrass habitat** are key examples. Source also lists wild pig, treeshrew, crested serpent eagle and Nicobar paradise flycatcher.
- Embedded graphic reports **over 8.5 lakh trees / 130 km²**, and **648 flora / 330 fauna species** for the cited forest context. These are source-reported proposal/biodiversity figures, not independently harmonised counts.
- Graphic contrasts a ZSI report of **117 scleractinian coral species** with an EIA claim about the Galathea Bay site; retain as a **disputed site/assessment claim**, not a resolved finding.
- **Shompen** hunter-gatherer foraging grounds and **Nicobarese** livelihoods/land rights; migration can pressure water, housing, health services and cultural continuity.
## Development and security
- Potential benefits: transshipment, trade connectivity, jobs and strategic maritime presence; actual gains depend on viability, skills and equitable benefit sharing.
- Dual-use infrastructure needs access control, surveillance, resilience and coordination of civilian/military activities; hypothetical risks do not establish that sabotage or interference has occurred.
- Tourism and ship recycling, if pursued, need carrying-capacity assessment and robust waste/hazardous-material controls.
## Transparency and decision framework
- Source criticises security-based RTI restrictions and public participation; treat claims about particular denials as its reported dispute, not proof that no clearance or consultation exists.
- **Alternatives → cumulative EIA → rights/community consultation → security-sensitive disclosure rules → enforceable safeguards → independent monitoring**.
- Balance strategic value with irreversible habitat loss, tribal welfare and disaster vulnerability; scrutinise both costs and claimed mitigation effectiveness.

topics.title: Preventive health and non-communicable diseases
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Causes and consequences
