- Major NCD groups: **cardiovascular diseases, cancers, diabetes and chronic respiratory disease**.
- Risks: tobacco, harmful alcohol use, unhealthy diet, inactivity, obesity, raised blood pressure, glucose/lipids; age, genetics, air pollution and social conditions also matter.
- Premature death/disability → productivity loss and household treatment spending → financial insecurity and pressure on health services.
- January 2025 source reports **65% of deaths**, versus **50% in 2010–13**, and an economic-loss projection **over ₹280 lakh crore by 2030** attributed to WHO. Different periods/methods and the projection's scope need checking; these are not observed 2030 costs.
## Prevention is broader than screening
| Stage | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Primary prevention | Tobacco control, healthier food/activity, cleaner environments |
| Early detection | Appropriate risk-based screening and diagnosis |
| Follow-up care | Referral, affordable treatment, adherence and rehabilitation |
- Strengthen **Ayushman health/wellness primary-care centres**, community outreach and trained teams; ensure tests lead to treatment, not just higher screening counts.
- AI-supported tools may assist validated screening; require accuracy, clinical oversight, privacy and workable referral pathways.
## January 2025 editorial proposals
- Subsidised private screening, especially **40–60-year-olds**, public/private partnerships and funding from health-related levies.
- Source describes **₹5,000 preventive-checkup deduction under section 80D** and proposes **₹15,000**. The increase is a recommendation, not a notified entitlement; tax eligibility also depends on the applicable regime/year.
- Awareness should communicate useful tests, risk factors and follow-up; indiscriminate testing can produce false positives and unnecessary costs.
## Implementation and Mains answer
- Barriers: rural access, affordability, workforce shortages, equipment, funding, interpretation and continuity of care.
- Public primary-care investment + affordable partnership delivery + community awareness; prioritise equity and cost-effective evidence-based prevention.
- Track disease control, avoidable complications, out-of-pocket spending and rural coverage alongside screening volume.
- PDF 'daily Mains' and practice questions are coaching exercises, not UPSC PYQs.

topics.title: India’s neighbourhood and strategic outlook
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 outlook: distinguish analysis from fact
- **China**: disengagement at particular LAC friction points does not settle the boundary or establish complete de-escalation. Competition includes infrastructure, regional influence and multilateral forums.
- **Bangladesh**: the post-Hasina transition cited by the source raises border, connectivity and diplomatic challenges; avoid labelling all citizens or institutions 'anti-India'.
- **Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan**: partners balance sovereign interests and multiple relationships. Ties with China do not by themselves prove loss of Indian influence.
- **Pakistan**: terrorism/security concerns and limited regional cooperation complicate engagement.
- **West Asia/Syria**: political transition, conflict spillovers and shifting regional influence affect energy, trade and diaspora interests; the source's predictions about Iran, Israel and Turkey are scenarios, not fixed outcomes.
## Cross-cutting risks
- Cyberattacks on critical infrastructure, government and businesses; protect systems, build response capacity and strengthen resilience.
- External shocks interact with domestic infrastructure, economic transitions and social cohesion; strategic influence needs credible domestic capacity.
## Policy response
- Respectful neighbourhood diplomacy, reliable project delivery, trade/connectivity, humanitarian support and people-to-people ties.
- Bilateral engagement and suitable regional forums (**BIMSTEC, SAARC**), while accounting for institutional constraints.
- Combine deterrence and border management with dialogue; diversify energy/supply chains and maintain strategic autonomy.
- Mains structure: **specific country/issue → Indian interest → cooperation + risk management → implementable response**.
- The source's speculative practice question about which neighbours are 'challenges' is not an objective permanent country classification or a UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: India–France defence and strategic partnership
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## Milestones and exercises
- Diplomatic relations **1948**; strategic partnership **1998**. Cooperation spans defence, space, counterterrorism and the Indian Ocean/Indo-Pacific.
- **Shakti — Army; Varuna — Navy; Garuda — Air Force**.
- **2016** agreement for **36 Rafale** aircraft for the IAF; distinguish it from the later Navy acquisition.
- Scorpene/Kalvari-class conventional submarines: **Mazagon Dock, India + Naval Group, France**. They are not nuclear submarines.
## January 2025 proposals and verified later milestones
- Source anticipated **26 naval Rafale** and **three additional Scorpene submarines**, with a combined reported value above **$10 billion**, subject to approval/contracting; a proposal is not a completed acquisition.
- **Rafale agreement signed 28 April 2025**: **22 single-seat + four twin-seat aircraft**, training, support and weapons; do not describe all 26 as identical carrier-capable variants. [Defence Ministry release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2124851&lang=2&reg=48).
- **INS Vaghsheer commissioned 15 January 2025**, not January 2024 as printed; see the common naval-platforms topic.
- Paris **AI Action Summit: 10–11 February 2025**, not 2024. [French Foreign Ministry](https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/presse-et-ressources/decouvrir-et-informer/actualites/sommet-pour-l-action-sur-l-intelligence-artificielle).
- Source graphic oversimplifies the return of French settlements: distinguish **1954 de facto transfer** and **1962 de jure transfer** rather than repeat 'all five returned in 1962'.
## Strategic significance and evaluation
- Carrier aviation, underwater capability, maritime interoperability and France's regional presence, including **Réunion**.
- Technology transfer, domestic manufacture and maintenance support can build capacity; judge actual local content/skills rather than assume imports equal self-reliance.
- Evaluate cost, delivery schedules, support dependence, interoperability and indigenous alternatives; maintain a multipolar approach and strategic autonomy.
- Do not memorise the PDF's generic 'Towed Artillery System' claim as a verified named bilateral procurement deal.

topics.title: UDISE+ and school education indicators
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## System
- **Unified District Information System for Education Plus**, Department of School Education and Literacy; online system introduced **2018–19**.
- Covers recognised schools: enrolment, teachers, infrastructure and other education indicators; supports RTE/NEP planning rather than replacing the RTE Act.
- National **student-wise data from 2022–23** differs from earlier school-level aggregate returns. **Earlier and later series are not strictly comparable.** From 2023–24, reporting also aligns with NEP's **5+3+3+4** stages. [Official report](https://dsel.education.gov.in/sites/default/files/statistics/report_in_PDF/udise_report_nep_23_24.pdf).
## Source figures: interpret carefully
- Enrolment: **25.18 crore (2022–23) → 24.80 crore (2023–24)**: decrease **0.38 crore**, about **1.5%**, not the PDF practice answer's 6% for these two years.
- Older graphic: **26.03 crore (2018–19), 26.45 (2019–20), 26.44 (2020–21), 26.52 (2021–22)**. The roughly 6% comparison uses an older-series baseline and must carry the methodology caveat.
- Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra cited for large enrolment declines; enrolment change and dropout rate are different indicators.
- Source says foundational dropout zero and secondary dropout highest. Zero in a reporting metric does not prove universal access/attendance. Demography, migration, deduplication and collection changes require examination before causal claims.
- Source incorrectly calls Classes 1–5 all of 'elementary': distinguish **primary 1–5** from the broader elementary stage.
## Definitions and governance
- **GER = all enrolled at a level, regardless of age ÷ population of the official age group × 100**; may exceed 100.
- Retention, dropout, enrolment and learning outcomes are distinct; reported retention gains cannot alone prove a scheme caused better learning.
- Low student-to-school ratios cited in Assam, Odisha and Karnataka; a low ratio may reflect remoteness/access needs, not simply waste.
- Responses: accurate student tracking with privacy safeguards, targeted teachers/facilities, transport and retention support, PM POSHAN/Samagra Shiksha, inclusion and learning assessment.

topics.title: Crop insurance: PMFBY, RWBCIS and technology
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 Cabinet decision
- **PMFBY + Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS)** continued through **2025–26**, with **₹69,515.71 crore for 2021–22 to 2025–26**, not a new one-year allocation.
- **Fund for Innovation and Technology (FIAT): ₹824.77 crore** for technology and more transparent assessment/settlement. [Cabinet release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2089249&lang=1&reg=3).
## Distinguish schemes
| Scheme | Core basis |
| --- | --- |
| PMFBY | Crop yield loss from covered risks |
| RWBCIS | Weather-index deviations, including rain/temperature/humidity/wind |
- Eligible farmers, including eligible tenants/sharecroppers, grow **notified crops in notified areas**; this does not automatically cover every crop everywhere.
- Crops: food crops (cereals, millets, pulses), oilseeds, annual commercial and horticultural crops.
| Farmer premium ceiling | Rate of sum insured |
| --- | --- |
| Kharif food/oilseed | 2% or actuarial rate, whichever lower |
| Rabi food/oilseed | 1.5% or actuarial rate, whichever lower |
| Annual commercial/horticultural | 5% or actuarial rate, whichever lower |
- State/government support covers the balance under scheme rules; premium rate is not the compensation percentage.
- Coverage subject to notifications: yield loss, eligible prevented sowing/localised calamities and specified post-harvest losses **up to 14 days**; war/nuclear and excluded preventable losses are not blanket-covered.
## Technology and Mains
- **YES-TECH — Yield Estimation System Based on Technology**: technology-assisted yield estimates; **WINDS — Weather Information Network Data Systems**: hyperlocal weather observations; National Crop Insurance Portal supports administration.
- Benefits: speed, assessment quality and transparency; challenges: basis risk, station quality, tenant documentation, awareness, delayed subsidy/claims and grievance redress.
- Combine reliable data with auditable assessment, timely funding, farmer access and effective appeals; technology alone does not remove basis risk.

topics.title: Fertilisers, DAP and subsidy reform
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## DAP and January 2025 package
- **Di-ammonium phosphate** supplies **nitrogen + phosphorus**; produced from ammonia and phosphoric acid. Phosphorus supports roots, flowering and seed formation.
- **1 January 2025 Cabinet decision** extended special DAP support **₹3,500/tonne over and above NBS**, from that date until further orders; previous package covered 2024. [Cabinet release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2089259&lang=2&reg=48).
## Subsidy architecture
| Mechanism | Distinction |
| --- | --- |
| Urea | Statutorily notified farmer MRP; government supports eligible cost gap |
| NBS | Fixed nutrient-based subsidy for phosphatic/potassic fertilisers; not urea |
| Fertiliser DBT | Subsidy paid to companies based on eligible verified retail sales, rather than ordinary cash transfer to every farmer |
- The PDF's '100% subsidy' means release of the approved subsidy amount under the payment mechanism, **not that fertilisers are free or 100% of sale price is subsidised**.
## Efficiency and sustainability
- **Neem-coated urea** reduces diversion and improves nitrogen-use efficiency; avoid indiscriminate overuse.
- **IFFCO nano urea/DAP** are promoted for efficient nutrient delivery; assess field evidence and agronomic recommendations before assuming complete replacement of conventional fertilisers.
- **PM-PRANAM** promotes balanced use/alternative nutrients and better soil health. Organic/biofertilisers and soil-informed dosing complement chemical nutrients.
- Trade-off: affordable inputs and food security versus fiscal cost, imbalanced N:P:K use, import exposure, pollution and degraded soil health.
- Link excessive nitrogen application with the common groundwater nitrate note; retain one main explanation of contamination there.

topics.title: Cowpea: crop characteristics and nitrogen fixation
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Prelims recall
- **Vigna unguiculata**, family **Fabaceae/Leguminosae**; drought-tolerant legume of tropical/subtropical regions.
- Names: **lobia** (Hindi), **thattapayaru** (Tamil); bush and climbing forms.
- Seeds vary in colour (white, cream, brown, black); source reports **20–25% protein** for the cited seed context, with fibre, minerals and low fat. Composition depends on variety and basis.
- Root-associated symbiotic nitrogen fixation supports soil fertility; useful for intercropping and food security in water-stressed settings.
- **CROPS space germination** uses cowpea; experiment details are consolidated in the space-sector topic rather than repeated here.

topics.title: INSV Tarini and Navika Sagar Parikrama
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Navika Sagar Parikrama-II: January 2025 position
- **Lt Cdr Dilna K. and Lt Cdr Roopa A.**, two-person/double-handed circumnavigation; began **2 October 2024 from Goa**.
- Source plan: about **23,000 nautical miles / 240 days**; targets are not the final voyage's measured totals.
- Route: **Goa → Fremantle (Australia) → Lyttelton (New Zealand) → Port Stanley (Falklands) → Cape Town (South Africa) → Goa**.
- Third leg departed Lyttelton **4 January 2025**, about **5,600 nautical miles** towards the Falklands. [Navy release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2090132&lang=2&reg=48).
## Map and operational lessons
- **Southern Ocean; Drake Passage; Cape Horn at South America's southern end**; powerful storms and difficult seas test navigation, repairs, emergency response and teamwork.
- Source cites potential **60-knot winds / 12-metre waves** for the leg; these are reported conditions/risks, not a guaranteed description of every day.
- Vessel: ocean-going sailing yacht with navigation, communications and safety systems. The PDF calls it **40 feet**, while its old graphic gives **55 feet**; do not learn the conflicting 40-foot specification.
- The inserted graphic describes the earlier **2017–18 six-woman voyage**, led by Vartika Joshi, not this two-officer expedition. Keep its crew and projected March 2018 return out of NSP-II facts.
## Mains / Ethics
- Women's operational leadership, endurance, training, mutual trust and public inspiration; port interactions support maritime outreach.
- Sailing achievement illustrates skills and inclusion, but is not by itself evidence of combat capability or proof that Agnipath caused this expedition.

topics.title: Europa and the search for habitable ocean worlds
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## World and mechanism
- **Europa**: Jupiter's icy moon with strong evidence for a salty subsurface ocean; **liquid water + usable chemical energy + suitable ingredients** underpin habitability, not proof of life.
- Tidal flexing can generate internal heat; water-rock reactions may support chemical energy. The PDF's idea that blocking heat from Jupiter's radiation necessarily removes ocean energy is misleading. [NASA](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/europa-clipper/2024/10/14/nasas-europa-clipper-mission-investigating-an-ocean-world-2/).
- Thick ice can hinder nutrient/oxidant exchange and future direct access while shielding the ocean from radiation; uncertainty about exchange is not a finding that life is absent.
## Missions: compare
| Mission | Role |
| --- | --- |
| NASA Europa Clipper | Launched October 2024; Jupiter orbit with repeated Europa flybys; investigate habitability, ice, ocean and geology |
| NASA Juno | Jupiter mission; close moon flybys and measurements, including microwave observations |
| ESA Juice | Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer; Jupiter's icy moons, particularly Ganymede |
- Clipper uses remote instruments, including radar; **it is not an ice-drilling mission and not a direct life-detection mission**.
- Galilean moons: **Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto**; Io highly volcanic, Ganymede largest moon with intrinsic magnetic field, Callisto heavily cratered.
## Ice estimates: retain date and model
- January 2025 source reports roughly **35 km** ice versus earlier **10–20 km** estimates; not a universal measured thickness.
- Later **27 January 2026 NASA report**: about **29 km** for the observed cold conductive shell under a pure-water model; salt or additional convecting layers change interpretation. Do not silently replace an old report with a new estimate. [NASA Juno measurement](https://www.nasa.gov/missions/juno/nasas-juno-measures-thickness-of-europas-ice-shell/).
- Radiation, uncertain ice properties and exchange pathways complicate exploration. Enceladus and Titan are other astrobiology targets, with different surface/ocean environments; they are not established inhabited alternatives.

topics.title: Polavaram: river linking and multipurpose water infrastructure
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Core facts
- Multipurpose national project on the **Godavari, Andhra Pradesh**, not on Krishna; envisages an **80 TMC diversion to the Krishna basin**.
- Planned **gross irrigation potential 4,36,825 ha**, **960 MW hydropower**, drinking water for **28.5 lakh people in 611 villages**. Gross/annual irrigation potential differs from physical command area. [Polavaram Project Authority](https://ppa.gov.in/WPSCore/Common/WebPages/Home/ProjectMap.aspx).
- Spillway design discharge about **50 lakh cusecs / 1,41,435 cumecs**. Source calls this 'world's highest'; treat superlative as unverified rather than a durable ranking.
- PDF simplifies dimensions to **54 m / 1.2 km / 48 radial gates**; distinguish dam, spillway and full-reservoir elevation when comparing engineering specifications. A '1-in-1000-year' flood is a probability concept, not a guarantee of no flood for 1,000 years.
## Benefits and costs
- Irrigation, drinking/industrial water, energy and basin connectivity; benefits depend on completion and operating rules.
- Forest/farm submergence, tribal displacement, backwater impacts, altered sediment/environmental flows and fisheries livelihoods.
- Mains: assess demand/alternatives, interstate effects, fair rehabilitation and compensation, ecological flows, dam safety and transparent technical monitoring.

topics.title: Tularemia / rabbit fever
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Agent and transmission
- **Francisella tularensis — bacterium**, not virus; zoonosis affecting animals and humans, notably rabbits, hares and rodents.
- Human exposure: **tick/deer-fly bites**, contact with infected animals, contaminated water/food, aerosols/dust and laboratory exposure; route determines manifestations.
- Fever, skin ulcers/lymph-node involvement, eye inflammation, sore throat or respiratory disease; can be severe.
- Antibiotics are used; source says no US vaccine available. Clinical treatment depends on appropriate medical assessment, not one generic remedy.
## January 2025 trigger and trap
- US surveillance: **2,462 cases during 2011–22**, incidence **56% higher than 2001–10**; highest incidence among **5–9-year-olds, older men, American Indian/Alaska Native persons and central-US residents**. These are surveillance patterns, not the only susceptible groups. [CDC MMWR](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/73/wr/mm735152a1.htm).
- Tick/deer-fly exposure is important in the US context; do not infer from the PDF practice answer that all other transmission routes/vectors are impossible in every region.

topics.title: Export Inspection Council and quality certification
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution
- **Statutory body under section 3, Export (Quality Control and Inspection) Act, 1963**; Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry; headquarters **Delhi**.
- Quality control, inspection and export certification help meet importing-country safety/quality requirements and support market access. [EIC](https://eicindia.gov.in/).
- Chairperson heads the Council; **Director of Inspection and Quality Control** is executive head.
- Regional **Export Inspection Agencies: Mumbai, Kolkata, Kochi, Delhi, Chennai**, with suboffices and accredited laboratories; distinguish agencies from the Council.
## Scope and January 2025 context
- Source reports a gap assessment of **food-testing infrastructure** for exports.
- Mandatory schemes apply to **notified products**, not all exports indiscriminately. Source examples: fish/fishery, dairy, honey, egg, meat/poultry, animal casings, gelatine, ossein/crushed bones and specified feed products.
- Voluntary certification serves other food/non-food products under applicable schemes/importer requirements.
- Mains: accredited testing, traceability, harmonised standards, capacity and faster credible certification reduce rejection and trade costs without weakening safety.

topics.title: Black-collared yellow catfish conservation
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Verified identity and news
- **Horabagrus nigricollaris**, endemic to the **Chalakudy River, Kerala**; endangered freshwater catfish with ornamental value.
- **ICAR-NBFGR's Centre for Peninsular Aquatic Genetic Resources, Kochi** reported a captive-breeding protocol on **3 January 2025**; programme began **2020**, with first-generation breeding, restocking and farmer collaboration. [ICAR](https://www.icar.gov.in/en/breakthrough-captive-breeding-endangered-black-collared-yellow-catfish-horabagrus-nigricollaris).
- The supplied PDF confuses this fish with a coexisting species and says it 'coexists with H. nigricollaris'; **H. nigricollaris is the target species itself**. Do not attribute its shorter-barbel/green-mottled description without resolving the species identity.
## Conservation and institution
- Threats: habitat loss, overfishing and a very restricted distribution; **ex-situ breeding complements in-situ river habitat protection**.
- Genetic diversity, disease control and appropriate restocking are crucial; releasing fish is not proof of a self-sustaining recovered population.
- **NBFGR**: ICAR bureau established **1983 at Allahabad/Prayagraj**; current headquarters **Lucknow**. Works on assessment/conservation of fish genetic resources and sustainable use.

topics.title: Left-wing extremism: security and governance
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Roots and geography
- Violent Maoist/Naxalite insurgency challenges constitutional authority; **Naxalbari uprising, West Bengal, 1967** is the historical origin reference. Ordinary lawful left political activity is distinct from armed extremism.
- Source's historical Red Corridor includes parts of **Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Bihar, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Kerala**; extent changes over time, so an old map is not a current affected-district list.
- **Jal–Jungle–Jameen** grievances: land dispossession, forest/resource access, exploitation, exclusion, weak local services and representation; insurgent coercion and ideology interact with these conditions.
## January 2025 trigger
- Embedded newspaper reports a **6 January 2025 Bijapur IED attack**, killing **eight security personnel and a civilian driver**, on personnel returning from Abujhmad operations; reported incident details remain dated.
- Forest terrain, intelligence gaps, illicit arms and route-security risks make operations difficult; falling aggregate violence does not eliminate local threat.
## SAMADHAN: 2017 doctrine
| Letter | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| S | Smart leadership |
| A | Aggressive strategy |
| M | Motivation and training |
| A | Actionable intelligence |
| D | Dashboard-based KPIs |
| H | Harnessing technology |
| A | Action plan for each theatre |
| N | No access to financing |
- Source cites specialised teams and **Operations Octopus, Double Bull, Chakrabandha (2022)** as operational examples; security-only measures cannot resolve all underlying grievances.
## Way forward
- Coordinated Centre/state planning, trained local police, intelligence sharing, lawful operations and protection of civilians.
- Land/forest rights, accountable services, education/jobs, local recruitment, democratic representation and credible surrender/rehabilitation routes build trust.
- Source **2021 Peace March**, 'Bastar maange hinsa se azadi', illustrates community demand for freedom from violence.
- Evaluate outcomes through sustainable safety and access to justice/services, not only encounters or area-clearing claims.

topics.title: Hazardous waste and the Bhopal legacy
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Bhopal: hazard, accountability and remediation
- **Night of 2–3 December 1984**: methyl isocyanate (**MIC**) release from Union Carbide India Ltd's pesticide factory, Bhopal; maintenance/process-safety failures and inadequate safeguards are central lessons.
- Acute respiratory/eye injury and enduring health/environmental burdens; source cites **over 5,000 deaths, about half a million affected and at least 30 tonnes released**. Counts depend on period/definition and should not be treated as one universally settled toll.
- Source legal timeline: **1989 $470-million settlement; 2010 convictions of seven UCIL officials for negligence**. Cleanup/compensation did not automatically resolve long-term health or contamination.
- Source **January 2025 waste-removal** discussion is a dated step, not proof that the whole site was fully remediated.
## Waste characteristics and methods
- Hazardous properties include **toxicity, ignitability, corrosivity and reactivity**; industrial processes, metal treatment and pollution-control residues are important sources.
- Source **7.66 million tonnes/year**, **83% from Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh**, and **25 cement plants** co-processing: inventory year is unspecified, so do not cite as current totals.
| Route | Key distinction / safeguard |
| --- | --- |
| Co-processing | Substitute eligible raw material/fuel in industrial processes, e.g. cement kilns; controlled quality/emissions |
| Material recovery | Copper from suitable cable residues; lead from batteries; prevent worker/community exposure |
| Energy recovery | Eligible oils/solvents; pollutant control and authorisation |
| Incineration | Controlled combustion; ash and flue gas still require treatment/monitoring |
| Pyrolysis | Thermal decomposition without oxygen / limited oxygen; oil, gas and char depend on feedstock |
- Syngas mainly **CO + H₂**, with other gases depending on process; hazardous-feedstock char is **not automatically safe soil amendment**.
## Rules and international movement
- **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016**, as amended. The PDF's 1989 rules are historical, not the sole operative framework. Separate e-waste/battery rules also matter. [Gazette](https://www.mpcb.gov.in/sites/default/files/hazardous-waste/rules/HWMRules2016_English.pdf).
- **Basel Convention**: transboundary movement and environmentally sound disposal, including prior-informed-consent controls; India a party since **1992**. [CPCB](https://cpcb.nic.in/NGTMC/HW/Final_Report_OA_804_2017.pdf).
- Source reduction, segregated authorised storage/transport, tracking, safe recovery and final disposal; cleaner technology, enforcement, emergency preparedness and health surveillance.
## MIC trap
- Colourless, volatile toxic chemical used in pesticide manufacture; water exposure can trigger a vigorous **exothermic reaction**.
- The PDF's claims 'no longer produced' and 'only one storage site worldwide' are unsupported/outdated; do not memorise them.

topics.title: Golden jackal and human-modified habitats
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Identity and ecology
- **Canis aureus**, canid; omnivorous opportunistic forager/scavenger, widespread across India and Eurasian habitats.
- Often more nocturnal near people; flexible behaviour elsewhere. Forms breeding pairs, shelters in dens/crevices and occupies riverine, grassland, wetland/mangrove and other suitable habitats.
- Source January 2025 context: adaptation to human-modified settings; coexistence requires waste control and habitat protection, not feeding wildlife.
- Habitat encroachment and poor management threaten local populations; scavenging and food-web roles support ecosystem functioning.
## Conservation and taxonomy traps
- Source status: **IUCN Least Concern; CITES Appendix III (India); Wildlife (Protection) Act Schedule I under the amended schedules**. IUCN risk category, trade listing and Indian legal protection measure different things. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1726/1/a1972-53.pdf).
- The PDF's North/East Africa distribution reflects older lumping: African golden-wolf populations were distinguished from **Eurasian golden jackal C. aureus**. [Genomic study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26234211/).

topics.title: Osteoporosis and bone health
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism and signs
- Bone resorption exceeds formation → reduced bone strength and microstructure → **fragility fracture risk**.
- Often silent until fracture; common sites **hip, wrist and vertebrae**. Vertebral fractures may cause back pain, loss of height and stooped posture.
- Age and hormonal changes matter: lower **estrogen**, particularly after menopause, or lower **testosterone**; other risks and medicines also contribute. [NIH NIAMS](https://www.niams.nih.gov/health-topics/osteoporosis?navPos=0).
## Prevention and care: exam level
- Appropriate nutrition, calcium/vitamin D adequacy, suitable weight-bearing/resistance activity and fall prevention.
- Clinical assessment may include bone-density measurement and prescribed medicines; supplements alone are not a universal cure.
- Link to ageing, primary-care prevention and affordable disability reduction; screening should be risk-appropriate.

topics.title: Panchayat Se Parliament and women’s representation
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Programme: January 2025
- **Panchayat Se Parliament 2.0**, inaugurated **6 January 2025** in the **Central Hall, Samvidhan Sadan**; **PRIDE, Lok Sabha Secretariat**, with **NCW and Ministry of Tribal Affairs**. [Parliament release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2090660&lang=2&reg=48).
- Source participants: **502 elected Scheduled Tribe women representatives from 22 states/UTs**; commemorates **Birsa Munda's 150th birth anniversary**.
- Training on constitutional provisions, parliamentary procedure and governance; recognition of grassroots work in education/rural development.
- Workshops and visits: Parliament, Samvidhan Sadan, Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya and Rashtrapati Bhawan; collective Preamble reading.
- Earlier **2024** edition reportedly involved **500 women sarpanches**.
## Mains value
- Reservation/elected presence must be backed by skills, access, autonomy, resources and freedom from proxy control.
- Peer learning and institutional exposure can build confidence; assess whether training improves actual participation, budgeting and public service delivery.

topics.title: Banihal Bypass and NH-44 connectivity
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 project facts
- **Banihal, Jammu and Kashmir**, on the **Ramban–Banihal stretch of NH-44**; source reports completion of a **four-lane, 2.35-km bypass**, **₹224.44 crore**.
- **Four viaducts, total 1,513 metres; three culverts**; bypasses town-market bottlenecks, aiding civilian/tourist and defence movement towards Kashmir.
## Route recall
- **NH-44: Srinagar → Kanyakumari**; an amalgamation of previous highway stretches, including old NH-7, rather than every section being old NH-7.
- Source length **3,745 km** is a dated/route-definition figure; avoid unverified world-rank '22nd'.
- Listed states/UTs: **Jammu and Kashmir → Punjab → Haryana → Delhi → Uttar Pradesh → Madhya Pradesh → Maharashtra → Telangana → Andhra Pradesh → Karnataka → Tamil Nadu**. Do not call all 11 'states'.
- Major cities along the corridor include Delhi, Agra, Hyderabad and Bengaluru.
- Geography link: transport corridors need slope/drainage safety, maintenance and disaster resilience, not only travel-time savings.

topics.title: Abdali / Hatf-II missile
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Prelims distinctions
- **Pakistan; short-range ballistic missile**, road-mobile, solid propellant; source associates development with **SUPARCO**.
- January 2025 source specifications: **single stage**, **180–200 km** range, **250–450 kg** payload, inertial guidance, reported **150 m CEP**, launch mass **1,750 kg**, length **6.5 m**, diameter **0.56 m**.
- These are source/version-specific figures, not a guarantee that every test/variant has the same range or payload; **CEP is a statistical accuracy measure**.
- Carried by **Transporter-Erector-Launcher (TEL)**; ballistic differs from BrahMos cruise-missile flight.
- Alleged Bangladeshi purchase consideration is a **reported proposal**, not an independently verified completed procurement.

topics.title: National anthem, state anthem and constitutional respect
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## National anthem
- **Jana Gana Mana**, Rabindranath Tagore; first sung at INC Calcutta session **27 December 1911**; adopted by Constituent Assembly **24 January 1950**.
- Full version about **52 seconds**; authorised short version about **20 seconds**. Source recalls the original poem's first stanza becoming the anthem.
- **Article 51A(a)**: respect the Constitution, its institutions, National Flag and National Anthem; constitutional duty, statutory offence and ceremonial protocol are distinct.
## Statute and protocol trap
- **Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, section 3**: intentionally preventing anthem singing or disturbing an assembly engaged in singing; up to **three years**, fine or both. The PDF's blanket 'skipping is punishable' is inaccurate. [India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1578/3/A1971-69.pdf).
- MHA's historical orders cover national salutes, civil/military investitures and designated formal functions; normally stand at attention, with relevant disability/exhibition exceptions. Use the applicable official order for present ceremonial requirements. [MHA orders](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/AnthemEnglish_140316.pdf).
## Tamil Nadu dispute: January 2025
- **Tamil Thai Vazhthu**, Sundaram Pillai's **1891 Manonmaniam**, designated Tamil Nadu state anthem in **2021**.
- Source assembly convention: state anthem at the start of the Governor's address; national anthem at the end. Raj Bhavan alleged disrespect; an allegation is not a judicial finding of a statutory offence.
- State symbolism and national respect can coexist; examine the exact act, intent and protocol before declaring illegality.

topics.title: Earthquakes, seismic waves and risk
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Focus, fault and waves
- Earthquake: sudden release of stored energy, often through **fault slip**; tectonic movement, volcanic processes and some human activities can trigger seismicity.
- **Focus/hypocentre**: origin inside Earth; **epicentre**: surface point vertically above it.
| Wave | Medium / motion |
| --- | --- |
| P, primary body wave | Fastest; compression; solids, liquids and gases |
| S, secondary body wave | Transverse; solids; cannot pass through liquid outer core |
| Love, surface wave | Horizontal side-to-side motion |
| Rayleigh, surface wave | Elliptical motion in a vertical plane |
- **P-wave shadow zone roughly 103°–142° angular distance from epicentre**; refraction through the core. Direct S waves absent beyond about **103°** because the outer core is liquid.
- Love waves generally faster than Rayleigh waves; surface waves can be highly destructive. Shaking damage also depends on depth, distance, soil and construction.
## Measurement and distribution
- **Seismometer** records motion; **magnitude** measures event size, while **Mercalli-type intensity** describes local effects (I–XII).
- Source's Richter '0–10' is not a fixed upper-bounded scale; modern large-earthquake reporting commonly uses moment magnitude.
- Major belts: **Circum-Pacific, Alpine-Himalayan, mid-ocean ridges**. Source approximate **81%/17%** shares are broad distribution claims with differing event definitions, not timeless exact proportions.
- Plate boundaries: convergence/subduction, transform sliding and divergence/spreading; earthquakes also occur within plates.
## January 2025 Indian map and interior
- Source-era BIS zones **II, III, IV, V**, with V highest; about **59%** land classified in moderate-to-very-high hazard zones. The graphic's older **Zone I** key should not be combined with the four-zone map. [NIDM explanation](https://nidm.gov.in/safety_earthquake.asp).
- These are the **January 2025 source-era classifications**, not a claim that later standards cannot change.
- **Crust + uppermost mantle = lithosphere** over weaker asthenosphere; mantle extends to about **2,900 km**; **liquid outer core**, **solid inner core**.
- Risk reduction: enforce appropriate building codes, retrofit critical facilities, map local soils, plan drills/emergency response and protect lifelines; hazard maps do not predict exact earthquake dates.

topics.title: World Gold Council and official gold reserves
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## Institution and functions
- **World Gold Council (WGC)**: gold-industry organisation, **1987**, headquartered **London**; represents major gold producers, promotes sustainable demand and use. It does **not regulate global gold prices or manage countries' official reserves**.
- Market development/standards; research (including **Gold Demand Trends**, quarterly reports); policy advocacy, new technological uses and investment-product development, including gold ETFs.
- Source January 2025 snapshot: **33 members**, markets representing about **75% of annual gold consumption**; membership/market coverage are dated figures.
## November 2024 reserve purchases
- Reported global central-bank **net purchases: 53 tonnes; RBI: 8 tonnes**. Monthly additions differ from total reserves and unreported purchases. [WGC January 2025 report](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/gold-focus/2025/01/central-bank-gold-statistics-november-2024).
- Embedded reserve ranking: **USA → Germany → Italy → France → Russia → China → Switzerland → India → Japan → Netherlands**. Graphic puts India at **846.76 tonnes**; undated snapshot, not a current ranking/stock.
- Mains use: reserve diversification and exposure to uncertainty; distinguish physical gold, gold ETFs, reserve holdings and annual demand.

topics.title: Tidal tails and galaxy evolution
topics.subject: Science and Technology
topics.markdown:
## Mechanism
- Close gravitational encounter/merger → **tidal forces** strip/distort outer **stars and gas** → elongated tails, sometimes leading/trailing features.
- Tails can outlast the merger and reveal interaction history; their material may form stellar clumps or tidal dwarf/ultra-diffuse systems.
- Examples: **Tadpole Galaxy; Mice Galaxies**. Not every interacting galaxy must have exactly two observable tails.
## NGC 3785: January 2025 news
- In **Leo**, about **430 million light-years** away; study reports an exceptionally long tail, **projected length ~390 kpc (~1.27 million light-years)**, **84 star-forming clumps** and a candidate nascent **ultra-diffuse galaxy at its end**. [Research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18811).
- Interpret as observational evidence/proposed formation mechanism, not proof that all ultra-diffuse galaxies share that origin.
- Source cites about **10% of an interacting galaxy's star formation** and **~1% globally** in tails; context-dependent estimates, not universal constants.

topics.title: Vembanad and lake-location recall
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## Vembanad-Kol system
- **Kerala**, across **Alappuzha, Kottayam and Ernakulam**; elongated coastal/backwater system with Arabian Sea outlets. **India's longest lake**, Kerala's largest; the PDF's unqualified 'largest lake in India' is misleading across lake types.
- Names: **Vembanad Kayal / Vembanad Kol**, **Punnamada** in Kuttanad, **Kochi Lake** in Kochi.
- Rivers include **Meenachil, Achankovil, Pampa and Manimala**; these are not the entire catchment. Ramsar description identifies **10 feeding rivers**.
- **Ramsar designation 19 August 2002**; listed **Vembanad-Kol wetland area 151,250 ha (1,512.5 km²)**. Do not equate the PDF's **2,033 km²** lake/system estimate with the Ramsar site boundary. [Convention on Wetlands](https://www.ramsar.org/news/india-designates-eleven-new-wetlands-international-importance).
- Islands: **Pathiramanal, Perumbalam, Pallippuram**; **Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary on eastern shore**.
- **Nehru Trophy Boat Race**, Punnamada; traditionally August, actual annual scheduling can change. Vallam Kali is the broader boat-racing tradition, not just this race.
## Ecosystem and livelihoods
- Fisheries/clams, rice cultivation, navigation, tourism, birds, flood buffering and groundwater recharge.
- Sewage/industrial and slaughterhouse/shrimp-processing pollution, encroachment/shrinking wetland and altered flows/salinity threaten water quality and livelihoods.

topics.title: Armed Forces Tribunal and judicial review
topics.subject: Indian Polity
topics.markdown:
## Jurisdiction and composition
- **Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007**; Ministry of Defence; specialised adjudication for personnel governed by **Army Act 1950, Navy Act 1957, Air Force Act 1950**.
- **Original jurisdiction** over service matters; **appellate jurisdiction** over court-martial orders, findings and sentences; remedies include setting aside unsustainable convictions and modifying sentences as authorised.
- Principal Bench **New Delhi**, regional benches; source lists Chandigarh, Lucknow, Kolkata, Guwahati, Chennai, Kochi, Mumbai, Jabalpur, Jaipur and Srinagar. Bench locations/territorial arrangements change; official list uses **Jammu**, so do not memorise source Srinagar as definitive. [AFT jurisdiction](https://aftdelhi.nic.in/index.php/home/jurisdiction).
- Benches have **judicial and administrative members**; source describes retired HC judges and senior armed-forces officers/JAG. Recruitment qualifications must be read under applicable Act/rules, not reduced to 'any retired officer'.
- **Procedure Rules, 2008**, proceedings in English; natural justice and statutory procedure.
## Appeal ≠ constitutional judicial review
- Act provides a statutory appeal route to the **Supreme Court subject to statutory conditions**.
- **High Court judicial review under Articles 226/227 remains**; **Balkrishna Ram (9 January 2020)** expressly affirms this. PDF's blanket 'only Supreme Court' excludes this distinction incorrectly. [Supreme Court judgment](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/4913/4913_2017_15_1501_19348_Judgement_09-Jan-2020.pdf).
- Source January 2025 discussion: additional benches for J&K/Himachal to reduce pendency; treat proposed expansion separately from actual constitution of a bench.
## Embedded tribunal recall
- **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, **Part XIV-A**: **Article 323A**, public-service administrative tribunals, Parliament; **323B**, tribunals for specified other matters, Parliament or state legislatures within competence.
- **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985**: CAT/SAT framework; do not assume every specialised tribunal, including AFT, is automatically created under 323A.
- Examples in graphic: CAT, NGT, ITAT, CESTAT, SAT (securities), water-disputes tribunals; old **COMPAT** label is historical because competition appeals moved to NCLAT.
- Expertise and access must accompany institutional independence, vacancies filled and constitutional review.

topics.title: Alaknanda and Panch Prayag
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## River route
- Garhwal Himalayas, **Uttarakhand**; meltwaters of **Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers**; approximately **190 km** to Devprayag.
- Main Ganga headstreams: **Alaknanda and Bhagirathi**; join at **Devprayag → Ganga**. Alaknanda contributes the larger flow, while Bhagirathi is traditionally treated as the source stream.
| Confluence, upstream → downstream | Alaknanda joins |
| --- | --- |
| Vishnuprayag | Dhauliganga |
| Nandprayag | Nandakini |
| Karnaprayag | Pindar |
| Rudraprayag | Mandakini |
| Devprayag | Bhagirathi |
- Valley links **Badrinath, Joshimath** and routes towards **Hemkund Sahib**; Hemkund is reached via a tributary-valley route, not situated on the main Alaknanda channel.
- Uttarakhand Char Dham: **Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri, Yamunotri**; not all four lie along the Alaknanda itself.
## Landslide-dam risk
- January 2025 source cites **IIT Roorkee** study: landslides can block the river, create temporary reservoirs, then breach and release flood pulses.
- Combine slope monitoring, drainage/land-use safeguards, upstream blockage detection and downstream warning/evacuation. See [landslides](landslides.html) through the main topic index if browsing across subjects.

topics.title: Common noctule bat and migration
topics.subject: Environment
topics.markdown:
## Species recall
- **Nyctalus noctula**; insectivorous mammal; narrow pointed wings, strong direct flight/steep insect-chasing dives; golden to dark-brown upper body, paler underside.
- Forest/tree hollows and some buildings/crevices; open-country/settlement foraging. Hibernates in winter; urban roosts important in parts of eastern Europe.
- Source distribution spans **Europe and temperate Asia**, with peripheral localities; **IUCN Least Concern** is the source status, not absence of local threats.
- Echolocation around **25 kHz**; this is **ultrasound**, above the usual ~20-kHz human limit. Some lower-frequency components may be audible; source's blanket '25 kHz heard by children' is unreliable.
## January 2025 migration study
- Common noctules exploit **warm tailwinds ahead of storm fronts**: temperature rises/pressure falls → departures → longer travel with lower energy use.
- Study tracked **71 females**, moving generally northeast from Swiss wintering areas; **no single fixed corridor**, feeding stops and almost **400 km in one night** recorded. Study tracked portions, not every individual's entire annual migration. [Max Planck study](https://www.mpg.de/23893833/bats-surf-storm-fronts-during-continental-migration).
- Ecological role: insect control; conservation use: predict migration windows and reduce wind-turbine collision mortality.

topics.title: BHARATPOL and INTERPOL cooperation
topics.subject: Internal Security of India
topics.markdown:
## Platform
- **CBI-developed**, launched **7 January 2025** by Union Home Minister; **CBI is NCB-New Delhi**, India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL.
- Single digital channel connects Indian law-enforcement agencies with CBI/INTERPOL cooperation: standard requests, faster intelligence sharing, notices, documents and training.
- Crimes: cybercrime, trafficking in persons/drugs/arms, financial fraud, terrorism/online radicalisation; cross-border data requests need lawful safeguards.
| Module | Recall |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | CBI/NCB and Indian agencies on one platform |
| INTERPOL Notices | Notice requests |
| Broadcast | Disseminate foreign assistance/intelligence requests |
| References | International investigative assistance |
| Resources | Documents and capacity building |
- The PDF misassigns Notice functionality to **Connect**; keep the modules distinct. [MHA/PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2099539&lang=2&reg=48).
## INTERPOL and notices
- **International Criminal Police Organization; 1923; Lyon, France**. Source states **196 members**; '195 other countries' is consistent with India being one of 196, but '195 total members' is outdated.
| Notice | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Red | Locate and provisionally arrest a wanted person for extradition/surrender or similar lawful action |
| Blue | Obtain identity/location/activity information |
| Green | Warning about persons posing a criminal threat |
| Yellow | Missing persons, often minors; identify persons unable to identify themselves |
| Black | Identify bodies |
| Orange | Warn of dangerous events/objects/materials/methods |
| Purple | Criminal methods, devices or concealment techniques |
| INTERPOL–UNSC special | Individuals/entities subject to UNSC sanctions |
- **Red Notice is not an international arrest warrant**; national law controls legal effect. [INTERPOL notices](https://www.interpol.int/How-we-work/Notices/), [official safeguards FAQ](https://www.interpol.int/content/download/15314/file/INTERPOL%20FAQ%20on%20Personal%20Data%20Safeguards.pdf).
- Institutional priorities in graphic: counter-terrorism, organised/emerging crime and cybercrime.

topics.title: Net-zero banking and financed emissions
topics.subject: Indian Economy
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 framework
- **Net-Zero Banking Alliance (NZBA)**: bank-led, **UNEP Finance Initiative-convened**, launched **2021**; voluntary alignment of lending/investment/capital-market portfolios with **net-zero by 2050 or sooner**, Paris goals.
- Targets for **2030**, intermediate milestones; priority to emissions-intensive energy, transport, agriculture and other sectors; annual **absolute emissions and intensity** reporting.
- CEO-signed commitment, member-bank Steering Group and UNEP FI secretariat support; source describes intermediary sector targets within **36 months**. Historical framework requirements changed later.
- Source January 2025 context: major US banks withdrawing; **no Indian bank member** reported at that time. Do not present this as current membership.
- **Financed emissions ≠ only office/branch emissions**; portfolio reductions should support real-economy transition. Offsets require credible quality and disclosure, not substitution for every reduction.
## Mains evaluation and later status
- Benefits: comparable targets, accountability and transition finance; limitations: voluntary enforcement, exits, inconsistent scope, greenwashing and undue offset reliance.
- **August 2025**: activities paused while members voted on transition to a framework. Today's official page presents **Net-Zero Banking Resources**, not a current member roster; the January alliance description is historical. [UNEP FI August update](https://www.unepfi.org/net-zero-banking/media/nzba-update-august-2025/), [resources](https://www.unepfi.org/net-zero-banking/).

topics.title: Crowd crush and stampede prevention
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## How crowd disasters develop
- Dense crowds + bottleneck/opposing flows/sudden stopping/barrier failure → pressure waves, falls or pile-ups → injury and **compressive/traumatic asphyxia**.
- Source types: **unidirectional** (same flow suddenly obstructed) and **turbulent/multidirectional** (flows converge/disordered pressure). A crush need not require irrational panic or running.
- Chest/upper-abdominal compression impairs breathing; head/neck/internal-organ injury and cardiac events also possible. Source **3–4 persons/m²** warning is not one universal safe/unsafe threshold; venue geometry and flow matter.
- Hazards: inadequate lighting/exits, stalls/parking narrowing paths, counterflows, weak structures, fire/electrical/LPG risks, poor communication and rumours.
- Impacts: deaths/disability, PTSD, income loss, medical/legal/compensation costs, infrastructure damage and loss of public trust.
## Prevention: capacity → flow → monitoring → response
- Assess venue carrying capacity, arrival/departure peaks and vulnerable groups; timed/ticketed entry where appropriate, separate ingress/egress and keep emergency access clear.
- Coordinated police/organiser command; route maps, multilingual public-address/signage, suitable barricades, CCTV and staff trained to relieve pressure early.
- Ambulances, medical teams, hospital links, evacuation drills; safe electrical wiring, LPG and fireworks controls. [NDMA safety guidance via PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=151549).
- **NDMA**, chaired by **Prime Minister**, statutory under **Disaster Management Act 2005**: policy/plans/guidelines; connect preparedness to **Sendai Framework**.
- Density sensors/LiDAR, RFID and drones may aid monitoring where lawful and reliable; privacy, accessibility, power/network backup and actionable thresholds matter. PDF's bioluminescent pavement/automatic colour-changing schemes are suggestions, not established NDMA mandates.
- Source's 'upcoming Asian Ministerial Conference with UNISDR' is recycled older material, not a January 2025 event announcement.

| 27 August 2003 | Nashik Kumbh, Maharashtra |

| 1 January 2022 | Vaishno Devi, Jammu and Kashmir |
| March 2023 | Indore temple stepwell-cover collapse; structural disaster, not simply crowd panic |

- Graphic tolls range from **12 to 340**, including an early **116** for Hathras; provisional and sometimes inconsistent counts are not settled final totals. Useful for comparing crowd/structure failures without memorising disputed precision.
- Supplied 'Daily Mains Question' is coaching practice, not a year-identified UPSC PYQ.

topics.title: Saudi floods and arid-region urban risk
topics.subject: India & World Geography
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 case
- Source reports heavy rain, thunderstorms and flooding in **Mecca/Makkah, Madinah and Jeddah**, Saudi Arabia; roads/buildings inundated, vehicles displaced, travel disrupted.
- Source rainfall snapshot: **Al-Shafiyah, Madinah 49.2 mm; Al-Basateen, Jeddah 38 mm**; accumulation period unspecified, so do not compare with annual rainfall.
- **National Center of Meteorology (NCM)** alerts; **Saudi Red Crescent Authority** preparedness. 'Unprecedented' is the article's description, not a verified historical record.
## Mechanism and mains application
- Arid climate does **not exclude flash flooding**: concentrated rainfall + rapid runoff/impervious surfaces + insufficient drainage → short-warning floods.
- **Mecca**: Kaaba/Hajj pilgrimage; **Jeddah**, Red Sea gateway/transport hub; pilgrimage demand raises exposure and evacuation complexity.
- Impacts: disrupted roads/tourism/business, damaged infrastructure, contaminated water/waterborne-disease risk and rescue demands.
- Actions: rainfall nowcasting, drainage/wadi-flow protection, resilient roads, public warnings, rescue/health coordination and safe drinking water.
- Climate change can increase intense-rain risk, but attributing this specific event requires evidence; the PDF alone does not establish causation or a region-wide trend.

topics.title: India–Afghanistan engagement
topics.subject: International Relations
topics.markdown:
## January 2025 diplomatic step
- **8 January 2025, Dubai**: Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri** met Taliban administration's acting Foreign Minister **Amir Khan Muttaqi**; an upgrade to Foreign Secretary-level contact after the **2021 Taliban takeover**, not the first India–Afghanistan meeting ever.
- Humanitarian assistance, Afghan needs, trade via **Chabahar, Iran**, connectivity and regional security. **Engagement did not constitute formal Indian recognition of the Taliban government** in this January context.
- **1950 Treaty of Friendship**; development links include **Salma/Afghan–India Friendship Dam, Herat; 218-km Zaranj–Delaram road; Afghan Parliament; Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health and Habibia School, Kabul**.
- Source graphic also cites **Pul-e-Khumri–Kabul 220-kV transmission line and Chimtala substation**, plus historical aid commitment **~$3.1 billion since November 2001**; not an annual aid figure.
## Interests → constraints → response
- Central Asian access and trade; Chabahar bypasses Pakistan-dependent overland access. Afghanistan is **landlocked**, not an Arabian Sea port state.
- Prevent terrorist safe havens; humanitarian goodwill and people-to-people links; avoid abandoning Afghan citizens amid political change.
- Constraints: Taliban governance/rights and security concerns, Pakistan transit/security factor and growing Chinese engagement.
- Practical response: conditional project delivery, aid with accountability, diplomatic channels and connectivity, without conflating contact with endorsement of domestic practices.

topics.title: Dam safety: institutions, engineering and risks
topics.subject: Governance in India
topics.markdown:
## Dam Safety Act, 2021
- Surveillance, inspection, operation and maintenance of **specified dams**; prevent failure disasters and strengthen institutional responsibility.
| Level | Institution / role |
| --- | --- |
| National | **NCDS**, policy/protocol/standard-setting; chaired by CWC Chairperson |
| National | **NDSA**, implement/enforce framework and specified dispute-resolution functions |
| State | **State Committee on Dam Safety**, policy oversight |
| State | **State Dam Safety Organisation**, surveillance, monitoring and safety work |
- **Section 5**: NCDS constitution. **Both NCDS and NDSA notified 17 February 2022**; the PDF's January 2025 blanket 'NCDS not constituted' claim conflicts with official records. Distinguish initial constitution, periodic reconstitution and operational gaps. [Jal Shakti release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1807799&lang=2&reg=48).
## Risks and safeguards
- Ageing/structural deterioration; seismic exposure (**Tehri**); inadequate staff/maintenance; extreme inflows; sedimentation/storage loss; interstate operation disputes (**Mullaperiyar, Kerala–Tamil Nadu**); **2019 Tiware breach, Maharashtra**.
- Dams support irrigation, hydropower, water supply and flood moderation, but cannot eliminate every flood.
- Source ranks India **third in large-dam ownership**, gives **over 5,000/~5,700 dams**, **75–80% over 25 years**, **~200/227/234 over 100 years** across text/graphics. Snapshots differ; don't combine into one current inventory. **75% irrigation dependent on dams** is an unverified scope claim.
- **NRLD**, CWC inventory; **DRIP**, rehabilitation with World Bank/AIIB support for relevant phases; **DHARMA**, Dam Health and Rehabilitation Monitoring Application. Digital records are not automatically continuous sensor measurements.
- Source earthquake-safety centre example: seismic assessment/research; do not infer a separate universal enforcement authority from its name.
- Inspect before/after monsoon and distress events; funded rehabilitation, trained staff, instrumentation, emergency action plans, downstream warning/drills, sediment management and climate-sensitive operating rules. Drones/IoT/satellite/AI complement engineering inspections.
## Structure recall from the graphic
| Type | How it resists load |
| --- | --- |
| Embankment | Compacted earth/rockfill, controlled permeability/core and drainage |
| Gravity | Concrete/masonry mass resists water pressure; sound foundation |
| Arch | Curved concrete transfers load to strong canyon abutments |
| Buttress | Sloping slab/face supported by buttresses; transfers force to foundation |
- **Crest** top; **heel** upstream base; **toe** downstream base; **spillway** controlled overflow; **outlet/sluice** release; **gallery** internal inspection/drainage passage; **freeboard** vertical gap above water level to crest. Permeable material allows flow, impervious material restricts it.

topics.title: Flamingo Festival and wetland ecotourism
topics.subject: Environment

## January 2025 event and locations
- Source scheduled **18–20 January 2025**, **Sullurpeta, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh**, returning after five years.
- Birdwatching/eco-tourism at **Nelapattu**, **B.V. Palem**, **Atakanithippa**, **Sri City** and nearby wetland sites; **Pulicat** landscape links Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. The source's 'over 200 bird species' is broad event-region richness, not a promise every visitor sees 200 species.
